39.19: Are you the one who makes the horse so brave and covers his neck with flowing mane?
39.20: Do you make him leap like a grasshopper? His haughty neighing inspires terror.
39.21: Exultantly he paws the soil of the valley, and charges the battle-line in all his strength.
39.22: He laughs at fear; he is afraid of nothing, he recoils before no sword.
39.23: On his back the quiver rattles, the flashing spear and javelin.
39.24: Trembling with impatience, he eats up the miles; when the trumpet sounds, there is no holding him.
39.25: At each trumpet blast he neighs exultantly. He scents the battle from afar, the thundering of the commanders and the war cry.
39.26: Is it your wisdom that sets the hawk flying when he spreads his wings to travel south?
39.27: Does the eagle soar at your command to make her eyrie in the heights?
39.28: She spends her nights among the crags with a needle of rock as her fortress,
39.29: from which she watches for prey, fixing it with her far-ranging eye.
39.30: Even her young drink blood; where anyone has been killed, she is there.

40.1: Still speaking to Job, Yahweh said:
40.2: Is Yahweh's opponent going to give way? Has God's critic thought up an answer?
40.4: My words have been frivolous: what can I reply? I had better lay my hand over my mouth.
40.5: I have spoken once, I shall not speak again; I have spoken twice, I have nothing more to say.
40.6: Yahweh gave Job his answer from the heart of the tempest. He said:
40.7: Brace yourself like a fighter, I am going to ask the questions, and you are to inform me!
40.8: Do you really want to reverse my judgement, put me in the wrong and yourself in the right?
40.9: Has your arm the strength of God's, can your voice thunder as loud?
40.10: Come on, display your majesty and grandeur, robe yourself in splendour and glory.
40.11: Let the fury of your anger burst forth, humble the haughty at a glance!
40.12: At a glance, bring down all the proud, strike down the wicked where they stand.
40.13: Bury the lot of them in the ground, shut them, every one, in the Dungeon.
40.14: And I shall be the first to pay you homage, since your own right hand is strong enough to save you.
40.15: But look at Behemoth, my creature, just as you are! He feeds on greenstuff like the ox,
40.16: but what strength he has in his loins, what power in his stomach muscles!
40.17: His tail is as stiff as a cedar, the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
40.18: His bones are bronze tubes, his frame like forged iron.
40.19: He is the first of the works of God. His Maker threatened him with the sword,
40.20: forbidding him the mountain regions and all the wild animals that play there.
40.21: Under the lotus he lies, he hides among the reeds in the swamps.
40.22: The leaves of the lotus give him shade, the willows by the stream shelter him.
40.23: If the river overflows, he does not worry: Jordan might come up to his mouth, but he would not care.
40.24: Who is going to catch him by the eyes or put poles through his nose?
40.25: Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook or hold his tongue down with a rope?
40.26: Can you put a cane through his nostrils or pierce his jaw with a hook?
40.27: Will he plead lengthily with you, addressing you in diffident tones?
40.28: Will he strike a bargain with you to become your slave for life?
40.29: Will you make a pet of him, like a bird, keep him on a lead to amuse your little girls?
40.30: Is he to be sold by the fishing guild and then retailed by merchants?
40.31: Riddle his hide with darts? Or his head with fishing spears?
40.32: You have only to lay a finger on him never to forget the struggle or risk it again!

41.1: Any hope you might have would be futile, the mere sight of him would overwhelm you.
41.2: When roused, he grows ferocious, who could ever stand up to him?
41.3: Who has ever attacked him with impunity? No one beneath all heaven!
41.4: Next I will talk of his limbs and describe his matchless strength-
41.5: who can undo the front of his tunic or pierce the double armour of his breastplate?
41.6: Who dare open the gates of his mouth? Terror reigns round his teeth!
41.7: His back is like rows of shields, sealed with a stone seal,
41.8: touching each other so close that no breath could pass between,
41.9: sticking to one another making an impervious whole.
41.10: His sneezes radiate light, his eyes are like the eyelashes of the dawn.
41.11: From his mouth come fiery torches, sparks of fire fly out of it.
41.12: His nostrils belch smoke like a cauldron boiling on the fire.
41.13: His breath could kindle coals, flame issues from his mouth.
41.14: His strength resides in his neck, violence leaps before him as he goes.
41.15: The strips of his flesh are jointed together, firmly set in and immovable.
41.16: His heart is as hard as rock unyielding as the lower millstone.
41.17: When he stands up, the waves take fright and the billows of the sea retreat.
41.18: Sword may strike but will not stick in him, no more will spear, javelin or lance.
41.19: Iron means no more to him than straw, nor bronze than rotten wood.
41.20: No arrow can make him flee, a sling-stone tickles him like hay.
41.21: Club seems to him like straw, he laughs at the whirring javelin.
41.22: He has sharp potsherds underneath, and moves across the slime like a harrow.
41.23: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron, he makes the sea fume like a scent burner.
41.24: Behind him he leaves a glittering wake -- a white fleece seems to float on the deeps.
41.25: He has no equal on earth, being created without fear.
41.26: He looks the haughtiest in the eye; of all the lordly beasts he is king.

42.1: This was the answer Job gave to Yahweh:
42.2: I know that you are all-powerful: what you conceive, you can perform.
42.3: I was the man who misrepresented your intentions with my ignorant words. You have told me about great works that I cannot understand, about marvels which are beyond me, of which I know nothing.
42.4: (Listen, please, and let me speak: I am going to ask the questions, and you are to inform me.)
42.5: Before, I knew you only by hearsay but now, having seen you with my own eyes,
42.6: I retract what I have said, and repent in dust and ashes.
42.7: When Yahweh had finished saying this to Job, he said to Eliphaz of Teman, 'I burn with anger against you and your two friends, for not having spoken correctly about me as my servant Job has done.
42.8: So now find seven bullocks and seven rams, and take them back with you to my servant Job and make a burnt offering for yourselves, while Job, my servant, offers prayers for you. I shall show him favour and shall not inflict my displeasure on you for not having spoken about me correctly, as my servant Job has done.'
42.9: Eliphaz of Teman, Bildad of Shuah and Zophar of Naamath went away to do as Yahweh had ordered, and Yahweh listened to Job with favour.
42.10: And Yahweh restored Job's condition, while Job was interceding for his friends. More than that, Yahweh gave him double what he had before.
42.11: And all his brothers and all his sisters and all his friends of former times came to see him. Over dinner in his house, they showed their sympathy and comforted him for all the evils Yahweh had inflicted on him. Each of them gave him a silver coin, and each a gold ring.
42.12: Yahweh blessed Job's latter condition even more than his former one. He came to own fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand she-donkeys.
42.13: He had seven sons and three daughters;
42.14: his first daughter he called 'Turtledove', the second 'Cassia' and the third 'Mascara'.
42.15: Throughout the land there were no women as beautiful as the daughters of Job. And their father gave them inheritance rights like their brothers.
42.16: After this, Job lived for another one hundred and forty years, and saw his children and his children's children to the fourth generation.
42.17: Then, old and full of days, Job died.

1.1: How blessed is anyone who rejects the advice of the wicked and does not take a stand in the path that sinners tread, nor a seat in company with cynics,
1.2: but who delights in the law of Yahweh and murmurs his law day and night.
1.3: Such a one is like a tree planted near streams; it bears fruit in season and its leaves never wither, and every project succeeds.
1.4: How different the wicked, how different! Just like chaff blown around by the wind
1.5: the wicked will not stand firm at the Judgement nor sinners in the gathering of the upright.
1.6: For Yahweh watches over the path of the upright, but the path of the wicked is doomed.

2.1: Why this uproar among the nations, this impotent muttering of the peoples?
2.2: Kings of the earth take up position, princes plot together against Yahweh and his anointed,
2.3: 'Now let us break their fetters! Now let us throw off their bonds!'
2.4: He who is enthroned in the heavens laughs, Yahweh makes a mockery of them,
2.5: then in his anger rebukes them, in his rage he strikes them with terror.
2.6: 'I myself have anointed my king on Zion my holy mountain.'
2.7: I will proclaim the decree of Yahweh: He said to me, 'You are my son, today have I fathered you.
2.8: Ask of me, and I shall give you the nations as your birthright, the whole wide world as your possession.
2.9: With an iron sceptre you will break them, shatter them like so many pots.'
2.10: So now, you kings, come to your senses, you earthly rulers, learn your lesson!
2.11: In fear be submissive to Yahweh;
2.12: with trembling kiss his feet, lest he be angry and your way come to nothing, for his fury flares up in a moment. How blessed are all who take refuge in him!

3.1: [Psalm Of David When he was fleeing from his son Absalom] Yahweh, how countless are my enemies, how countless those who rise up against me,
3.2: how countless those who say of me, 'No salvation for him from his God!'Pause
3.3: But you, Yahweh, the shield at my side, my glory, you hold my head high.
3.4: I cry out to Yahweh; he answers from his holy mountain.Pause
3.5: As for me, if I lie down and sleep, I shall awake, for Yahweh sustains me.
3.6: I have no fear of people in their thousands upon thousands, who range themselves against me wherever I turn.
3.7: Arise, Yahweh, rescue me, my God! You strike all my foes across the face, you break the teeth of the wicked.
3.8: In Yahweh is salvation, on your people, your blessing!Pause

4.1: [For the choirmaster For strings Psalm Of David] When I call, answer me, God, upholder of my right. In my distress you have set me at large; take pity on me and hear my prayer!
4.2: Children of men, how long will you be heavy of heart, why love what is vain and chase after illusions?Pause
4.3: Realise that Yahweh performs wonders for his faithful, Yahweh listens when I call to him.
4.4: Be careful not to sin, speak in your hearts, and on your beds keep silence.Pause
4.5: Loyally offer sacrifices, and trust in Yahweh.
4.6: Many keep saying, 'Who will put happiness before our eyes?' Let the light of your face shine on us. Yahweh,
4.7: to my heart you are a richer joy than all their corn and new wine.
4.8: In peace I lie down and at once fall asleep, for it is you and none other, Yahweh, who make me rest secure.

5.1: [For the choirmaster For flutes Psalm Of David] Give ear to my words, Yahweh, spare a thought for my sighing.
5.2: Listen to my cry for help, my King and my God! To you I pray,
5.3: Yahweh. At daybreak you hear my voice; at daybreak I lay my case before you and fix my eyes on you.
5.4: You are not a God who takes pleasure in evil, no sinner can be your guest.
5.5: Boasters cannot stand their ground under your gaze. You hate evil-doers,
5.6: liars you destroy; the violent and deceitful Yahweh detests.
5.7: But, so great is your faithful love, I may come into your house, and before your holy temple bow down in reverence of you.
5.8: In your saving justice, Yahweh, lead me, because of those who lie in wait for me; make your way plain before me.
5.9: Not a word from their lips can be trusted, through and through they are destruction, their throats are wide -- open graves, their tongues seductive.
5.10: Lay the guilt on them, God, make their intrigues their own downfall; for their countless offences, thrust them from you, since they have rebelled against you.
5.11: But joy for all who take refuge in you, endless songs of gladness! You shelter them, they rejoice in you, those who love your name.
5.12: It is you who bless the upright, Yahweh, you surround them with favour as with a shield.

6.1: [For the choirmaster For strings For the octachord Psalm Of David] Yahweh, let your rebuke to me not be in anger, your punishment not in the heat of wrath.
6.2: Have pity on me, Yahweh, for I am fading away. Heal me, Yahweh, my bones are shaken,
6.3: my spirit is shaken to its very depths. But you, Yahweh . . . how long?
6.4: Yahweh, relent and save my life rescue me because of your faithful love,
6.5: for in death there is no remembrance of you; who could sing your praises in Sheol?
6.6: I am worn out with groaning, every night I drench my pillow and soak my bed with tears.
6.7: My eyes waste away with vexation. Arrogance from all my foes!
6.8: Away from me, all evil-doers! For Yahweh has heard the sound of my weeping,
6.9: Yahweh has heard my pleading. Yahweh will accept my prayer.
6.10: Let all my enemies be put to confusion, shaken to their depths, let them retreat in sudden confusion.

7.1: [Lament Of David Which he sang to Yahweh about Cush the Benjaminite] Yahweh my God, I take refuge in you, save me from all my pursuers and rescue me,
7.2: or he will savage me like a lion, carry me off with no one to rescue me.
7.3: Yahweh my God, if I have done this: if injustice has stained my hands,
7.4: if I have repaid my ally with treachery or spared one who attacked me unprovoked,
7.5: may an enemy hunt me down and catch me, may he trample my life into the ground and crush my vital parts into the dust.Pause
7.6: Arise, Yahweh, in your anger, rise up against the arrogance of my foes. Awake, my God, you demand judgement.
7.7: Let the assembly of nations gather round you; return above it on high!
7.8: (Yahweh judges the nations.) Judge me, Yahweh, as my uprightness and my integrity deserve.
7.9: Put an end to the malice of the wicked, make the upright stand firm, you who discern hearts and minds, God the upright.
7.10: God is a shield that protects me, saving the honest of heart.
7.11: God is an upright judge, slow to anger, but a God at all times threatening
7.12: for those who will not repent. Let the enemy whet his sword, draw his bow and make ready;
7.13: but he is making ready instruments of death for himself and tipping his arrows with fire;
7.14: look at him: pregnant with malice, conceiving spite, he gives birth to treachery.
7.15: He digs a trap, scoops it out, but he falls into the snare he made himself.
7.16: His spite recoils on his own head, his brutality falls back on his own skull.
7.17: I thank Yahweh for his saving justice. I sing to the name of the Most High.

8.1: [For the choirmaster On the . . . of Gath Psalm Of David] Yahweh our Lord, how majestic is your name throughout the world! Whoever keeps singing of your majesty higher than the heavens,
8.2: even through the mouths of children, or of babes in arms, you make him a fortress, firm against your foes, to subdue the enemy and the rebel.
8.3: I look up at your heavens, shaped by your fingers, at the moon and the stars you set firm-
8.4: what are human beings that you spare a thought for them, or the child of Adam that you care for him?
8.5: Yet you have made him little less than a god, you have crowned him with glory and beauty,
8.6: made him lord of the works of your hands, put all things under his feet,
8.7: sheep and cattle, all of them, and even the wild beasts,
8.8: birds in the sky, fish in the sea, when he makes his way across the ocean.
8.9: Yahweh our Lord, how majestic your name throughout the world!

9.1: [For the choirmaster On oboe and harp Psalm Of David] I thank you, Yahweh, with my whole heart, I recount all your wonders,
9.2: I rejoice and delight in you, I sing to your name, Most High.
9.3: My enemies are in retreat, they stumble and perish at your presence,
9.4: for you have given fair judgement in my favour, seated on your throne as upright judge.
9.5: You have rebuked the nations, destroyed the wicked, blotted out their name for ever and ever;
9.6: the enemy is wiped out -- mere ruins for ever -- you have annihilated their cities, their memory has perished. See,
9.7: Yahweh is enthroned for ever, keeping his throne firm for judgement;
9.8: he will himself judge the world in uprightness, will give a true verdict on the nations.
9.9: May Yahweh be a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble!
9.10: Those who revere your name can rely on you, you never desert those who seek you, Yahweh.
9.11: Sing to Yahweh who dwells in Zion, tell the nations his mighty deeds,
9.12: for the avenger of blood does not forget them, he does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.
9.13: Have pity on me, Yahweh, see my affliction, pull me back from the gates of death,
9.14: that I may recount all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion and rejoice in your salvation.
9.15: The nations have fallen into the trap they made, their feet caught in the snare they laid.
9.16: Yahweh has made himself known, given judgement, he has ensnared the wicked in the work of their own hands.Muted music Pause
9.17: May the wicked turn away to Sheol, all the nations forgetful of God.
9.18: For the needy is not forgotten for ever, not for ever does the hope of the poor come to nothing.
9.19: Arise, Yahweh; human strength shall not prevail. The nations shall stand trial before you.
9.20: Strike them with terror, Yahweh; the nations shall know that they are no more than human!Pause

10.1: Why, Yahweh, do you keep so distant, stay hidden in times of trouble?
10.2: In his pride the wicked hunts down the weak, who is caught in the schemes he devises.
10.3: The wicked is proud of his inmost desires, by his blasphemies the grasping spurns Yahweh,
10.4: the wicked in his arrogance does not look very far; 'There is no God,' is his only thought.
10.5: In all circumstances his step is assured; your judgements are above his head. His rivals? He scoffs at them all.
10.6: He says in his heart, 'I shall never be shaken,' free of trouble himself,
10.7: he wishes it on others. His speech is full of lies and browbeating, under his tongue lurk spite and wickedness.
10.8: In the undergrowth he lies in ambush, in his hiding-place he murders the innocent. He watches intently for the downtrodden,
10.9: lurking unseen like a lion in his lair, lurking to pounce on the poor; he pounces on him and drags him off in his net.
10.10: He keeps watch, crouching down low, the poor wretch falls into his clutches;
10.11: he says in his heart, 'God forgets, he has turned away his face to avoid seeing the end.'
10.12: Rise, Yahweh! God, raise your hand, do not forget the afflicted!
10.13: Why should the wicked spurn God, assuring himself you will never follow it up?
10.14: You have seen for yourself the trouble and vexation, you watch so as to take it in hand. The oppressed relies on you; you are the only recourse of the orphan.
10.15: Break the arm of the wicked and evil, seek out wickedness till there is none left to be found.
10.16: Yahweh is king for ever and ever, the heathen has vanished from his country.
10.17: Yahweh, you listen to the laments of the poor, you give them courage, you grant them a hearing,
10.18: to give judgement for the orphaned and exploited, so that earthborn humans may strike terror no more.

11.1: [For the choirmaster Of David] In Yahweh I have found refuge. How can you say to me, 'Bird, flee to your mountain?
11.2: 'For look, the wicked are drawing their bows, fitting their arrows to the string to shoot honest men from the shadows.
11.3: If the foundations fall to ruin, what can the upright do?'
11.4: Yahweh in his holy temple! Yahweh, his throne is in heaven; his eyes watch over the world, his gaze scrutinises the children of Adam.
11.5: Yahweh examines the upright and the wicked, the lover of violence he detests.
11.6: He will rain down red-hot coals, fire and sulphur on the wicked, a scorching wind will be their lot.
11.7: For Yahweh is upright and loves uprightness, the honest will ever see his face.

12.1: [For the choirmaster On the octachord Psalm Of David] Help, Yahweh! No one loyal is left, the faithful have vanished from among the children of Adam.
12.2: Friend tells lies to friend, and, smooth-tongued, speaks from an insincere heart.
12.3: May Yahweh cut away every smooth lip, every boastful tongue,
12.4: those who say, 'In our tongue lies our strength, our lips are our allies; who can master us?'
12.5: 'For the poor who are plundered, the needy who groan, now will I act,' says Yahweh, 'I will grant salvation to those who sigh for it.'
12.6: Yahweh's promises are promises unalloyed, natural silver which comes from the earth seven times refined.
12.7: You, Yahweh, will watch over them, you will protect them from that brood for ever.
12.8: The wicked will scatter in every direction, as the height of depravity among the children of Adam.

13.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] How long, Yahweh, will you forget me? For ever? How long will you turn away your face from me?
13.2: How long must I nurse rebellion in my soul, sorrow in my heart day and night? How long is the enemy to domineer over me?
13.3: Look down, answer me, Yahweh my God! Give light to my eyes or I shall fall into the sleep of death.
13.4: Or my foe will boast, 'I have overpowered him,' and my enemy have the joy of seeing me stumble.
13.5: As for me, I trust in your faithful love, Yahweh. Let my heart delight in your saving help, let me sing to Yahweh for his generosity to me, let me sing to the name of Yahweh the Most High!

14.1: [For the choirmaster Of David] The fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God.' Their deeds are corrupt and vile, not one of them does right.
14.2: Yahweh looks down from heaven at the children of Adam. To see if a single one is wise, a single one seeks God.
14.3: All have turned away, all alike turned sour, not one of them does right, not a single one.
14.4: Are they not aware, all these evil-doers? They are devouring my people, this is the bread they eat, and they never call to Yahweh.
14.5: They will be gripped with fear, where there is no need for fear, for God takes the side of the upright;
14.6: you may mock the plans of the poor, but Yahweh is their refuge.
14.7: Who will bring from Zion salvation for Israel? When Yahweh brings his people home, what joy for Jacob, what happiness for Israel!

15.1: [Psalm Of David] Yahweh, who can find a home in your tent, who can dwell on your holy mountain?
15.2: Whoever lives blamelessly, who acts uprightly, who speaks the truth from the heart,
15.3: who keeps the tongue under control, who does not wrong a comrade, who casts no discredit on a neighbour,
15.4: who looks with scorn on the vile, but honours those who fear Yahweh, who stands by an oath at any cost,
15.5: who asks no interest on loans, who takes no bribe to harm the innocent. No one who so acts can ever be shaken.

16.1: [In a quiet voice Of David] Protect me, O God, in you is my refuge.
16.2: To Yahweh I say, 'You are my Lord, my happiness is in none
16.3: of the sacred spirits of the earth.' They only take advantage of all who love them.
16.4: People flock to their teeming idols. Never shall I pour libations to them! Never take their names on my lips.
16.5: My birthright, my cup is Yahweh; you, you alone, hold my lot secure.
16.6: The measuring-line marks out for me a delightful place, my birthright is all I could wish.
16.7: I bless Yahweh who is my counsellor, even at night my heart instructs me.
16.8: I keep Yahweh before me always, for with him at my right hand, nothing can shake me.
16.9: So my heart rejoices, my soul delights, my body too will rest secure,
16.10: for you will not abandon me to Sheol, you cannot allow your faithful servant to see the abyss.
16.11: You will teach me the path of life, unbounded joy in your presence, at your right hand delight for ever.

17.1: [Prayer Of David] Listen, Yahweh, to an upright cause, pay attention to my cry, lend an ear to my prayer, my lips free from deceit.
17.2: From your presence will issue my vindication, your eyes fixed on what is right.
17.3: You probe my heart, examine me at night, you test me by fire and find no evil. I have not sinned with my mouth
17.4: as most people do. I have treasured the word from your lips,
17.5: my steps never stray from the paths you lay down, from your tracks; so my feet never stumble.
17.6: I call upon you, God, for you answer me; turn your ear to me, hear what I say.
17.7: Show the evidence of your faithful love, saviour of those who hope in your strength against attack.
17.8: Guard me as the pupil of an eye, shelter me in the shadow of your wings
17.9: from the presence of the wicked who would maltreat me; deadly enemies are closing in on me.
17.10: Engrossed in themselves they are mouthing arrogant words.
17.11: They are advancing against me, now they are closing in, watching for the chance to hurl me to the ground,
17.12: like a lion preparing to pounce, like a young lion crouching in ambush.
17.13: Arise, Yahweh, confront him and bring him down, with your sword save my life from the wicked,
17.14: Yahweh, from mortals, by your hand, from mortals whose part in life is in this world. You fill their bellies from your store, their children will have all they desire, and leave their surplus to their children.
17.15: But I in my uprightness will see your face, and when I awake I shall be filled with the vision of you.

18.1: [For the choirmaster Of David, the servant of Yahweh, who addressed the words of this song to Yahweh when Yahweh had delivered him from all his enemies and from the clutches of Saul. He said:] I love you, Yahweh, my strength (my Saviour, you have saved me from violence).
18.2: Yahweh is my rock and my fortress, my deliverer is my God. I take refuge in him, my rock, my shield, my saving strength, my stronghold, my place of refuge.
18.3: I call to Yahweh who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my foes.
18.4: With Death's breakers closing in on me, Belial's torrents ready to swallow me,
18.5: Sheol's snares every side of me, Death's traps lying ahead of me,
18.6: I called to Yahweh in my anguish, I cried for help to my God; from his Temple he heard my voice, my cry came to his ears.
18.7: Then the earth quaked and rocked, the mountains' foundations shuddered, they quaked at his blazing anger.
18.8: Smoke rose from his nostrils, from his mouth devouring fire (coals were kindled at it).
18.9: He parted the heavens and came down, a storm-cloud underneath his feet;
18.10: riding one of the winged creatures, he flew, soaring on the wings of the wind.
18.11: His covering he made the darkness, his pavilion dark waters and dense cloud.
18.12: A brightness lit up before him, hail and blazing fire.
18.13: Yahweh thundered from the heavens, the Most High made his voice heard.
18.14: He shot his arrows and scattered them, he hurled his lightning and routed them.
18.15: The very springs of ocean were exposed, the world's foundations were laid bare, at your roaring, Yahweh, at the blast of breath from your nostrils!
18.16: He reached down from on high, snatched me up, pulled me from the watery depths,
18.17: rescued me from my mighty foe, from my enemies who were stronger than I.
18.18: They assailed me on my day of disaster but Yahweh was there to support me;
18.19: he freed me, set me at large, he rescued me because he loves me.
18.20: Yahweh rewards me for my uprightness, as my hands are pure, so he repays me,
18.21: since I have kept the ways of Yahweh, and not fallen away from my God.
18.22: His judgements are all before me, his statutes I have not put away from me.
18.23: I am blameless before him, I keep myself clear of evil.
18.24: So Yahweh repaid me for acting uprightly because he could see I was pure.
18.25: You are faithful to the faithful, blameless with the blameless,
18.26: sincere to the sincere, but cunning to the crafty,
18.27: you save a people that is humble and humiliate those with haughty looks.
18.28: Yahweh, you yourself are my lamp, my God lights up my darkness;
18.29: with you I storm the rampart, with my God I can scale any wall.
18.30: This God, his way is blameless; the word of Yahweh is refined in the furnace, for he alone is the shield of all who take refuge in him.
18.31: For who is God but Yahweh, who is a rock but our God?
18.32: This God who girds me with strength, who makes my way free from blame,
18.33: who makes me as swift as a deer and sets me firmly on the heights,
18.34: who trains my hands for battle, my arms to bend a bow of bronze.
18.35: You give me your invincible shield (your right hand upholds me) you never cease to listen to me,
18.36: you give me the strides of a giant, give me ankles that never weaken.
18.37: I pursue my enemies and overtake them, not turning back till they are annihilated;
18.38: I strike them down and they cannot rise, they fall, they are under my feet.
18.39: You have girded me with strength for the fight, bent down my assailants beneath me,
18.40: made my enemies retreat before me; and those who hate me I destroy.
18.41: They cry out, there is no one to save; to Yahweh, but no answer comes.
18.42: I crumble them like dust before the wind, trample them like the mud of the streets.
18.43: You free me from the quarrels of my people, you place me at the head of the nations, a people I did not know are now my servants;
18.44: foreigners come wooing my favour, no sooner do they hear than they obey me;
18.45: foreigners grow faint of heart, they come trembling out of their fastnesses.
18.46: Life to Yahweh! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be the God of my salvation,
18.47: the God who gives me vengeance, and subjects whole peoples to me,
18.48: who rescues me from my raging enemies. You lift me high above those who attack me, you deliver me from the man of violence.
18.49: For this I will praise you, Yahweh, among the nations, and sing praise to your name.
18.50: He saves his king time after time, displays his faithful love for his anointed, for David and his heirs for ever.

19.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] The heavens declare the glory of God, the vault of heaven proclaims his handiwork,
19.2: day discourses of it to day, night to night hands on the knowledge.
19.3: No utterance at all, no speech, not a sound to be heard,
19.4: but from the entire earth the design stands out, this message reaches the whole world. High above, he pitched a tent for the sun,
19.5: who comes forth from his pavilion like a bridegroom, delights like a champion in the course to be run.
19.6: Rising on the one horizon he runs his circuit to the other, and nothing can escape his heat.
19.7: The Law of Yahweh is perfect, refreshment to the soul; the decree of Yahweh is trustworthy, wisdom for the simple.
19.8: The precepts of Yahweh are honest, joy for the heart; the commandment of Yahweh is pure, light for the eyes.
19.9: The fear of Yahweh is pure, lasting for ever; the judgements of Yahweh are true, upright, every one,
19.10: more desirable than gold, even than the finest gold; his words are sweeter than honey, that drips from the comb.
19.11: Thus your servant is formed by them; observing them brings great reward.
19.12: But who can detect his own failings? Wash away my hidden faults.
19.13: And from pride preserve your servant, never let it be my master. So shall I be above reproach, free from grave sin.
19.14: May the words of my mouth always find favour, and the whispering of my heart, in your presence, Yahweh, my rock, my redeemer.

20.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] May Yahweh answer you in time of trouble, may the name of the God of Jacob protect you!
20.2: May he send you help from the sanctuary, give you support from Zion!
20.3: May he remember all your sacrifices and delight in your burnt offerings! Pause
20.4: May he grant you your heart's desire and crown all your plans with success!
20.5: So that with joy we can hail your victory and draw up our ranks in the name of our God. May Yahweh grant all your petitions.
20.6: Now I know that Yahweh gives victory to his anointed. He will respond from his holy heavens with great deeds of victory from his right hand.
20.7: Some call on chariots, some on horses, but we on the name of Yahweh our God.
20.8: They will crumple and fall, while we stand upright and firm.
20.9: Yahweh, save the king, answer us when we call.

21.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] Yahweh, the king rejoices in your power; How your saving help fills him with joy!
21.2: You have granted him his heart's desire, not denied him the prayer of his lips.Pause
21.3: For you come to meet him with blessings of prosperity, put a crown of pure gold on his head.
21.4: He has asked for life, you have given it him, length of days for ever and ever.
21.5: Great his glory through your saving help; you invest him with splendour and majesty.
21.6: You confer on him everlasting blessings, you gladden him with the joy of your presence.
21.7: For the king puts his trust in Yahweh; the faithful love of the Most High will keep him from falling.
21.8: Your hand will reach all your enemies, your right hand all who hate you.
21.9: You will hurl them into a blazing furnace on the day when you appear; Yahweh will engulf them in his anger, and fire will devour them.
21.10: You will purge the earth of their descendants, the human race of their posterity.
21.11: They have devised evil against you but, plot as they may, they will not succeed,
21.12: since you will make them turn tail, by shooting your arrows in their faces.
21.13: Rise, Yahweh, in your power! We will sing and make music in honour of your strength.

22.1: [For the choirmaster To 'the Doe of the Dawn' Psalm Of David] My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? The words of my groaning do nothing to save me.
22.2: My God, I call by day but you do not answer, at night, but I find no respite.
22.3: Yet you, the Holy One, who make your home in the praises of Israel,
22.4: in you our ancestors put their trust, they trusted and you set them free.
22.5: To you they called for help and were delivered; in you they trusted and were not put to shame.
22.6: But I am a worm, less than human, scorn of mankind, contempt of the people;
22.7: all who see me jeer at me, they sneer and wag their heads,
22.8: 'He trusted himself to Yahweh, let Yahweh set him free! Let him deliver him, as he took such delight in him.'
22.9: It was you who drew me from the womb and soothed me on my mother's breast.
22.10: On you was I cast from my birth, from the womb I have belonged to you.
22.11: Do not hold aloof, for trouble is upon me, and no one to help me!
22.12: Many bulls are encircling me, wild bulls of Bashan closing in on me.
22.13: Lions ravening and roaring open their jaws at me.
22.14: My strength is trickling away, my bones are all disjointed, my heart has turned to wax, melting inside me.
22.15: My mouth is dry as earthenware, my tongue sticks to my jaw. You lay me down in the dust of death.
22.16: A pack of dogs surrounds me, a gang of villains closing in on me as if to hack off my hands and my feet.
22.17: I can count every one of my bones, while they look on and gloat;
22.18: they divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.
22.19: Yahweh, do not hold aloof! My strength, come quickly to my help,
22.20: rescue my soul from the sword, the one life I have from the grasp of the dog!
22.21: Save me from the lion's mouth, my poor life from the wild bulls' horns!
22.22: I shall proclaim your name to my brothers, praise you in full assembly:
22.23: 'You who fear Yahweh, praise him! All the race of Jacob, honour him! Revere him, all the race of Israel!'
22.24: For he has not despised nor disregarded the poverty of the poor, has not turned away his face, but has listened to the cry for help.
22.25: Of you is my praise in the thronged assembly, I will perform my vows before all who fear him.
22.26: The poor will eat and be filled, those who seek Yahweh will praise him, 'May your heart live for ever.'
22.27: The whole wide world will remember and return to Yahweh, all the families of nations bow down before him.
22.28: For to Yahweh, ruler of the nations, belongs kingly power!
22.29: All who prosper on earth will bow before him, all who go down to the dust will do reverence before him. And those who are dead,
22.30: their descendants will serve him, will proclaim his name to generations
22.31: still to come; and these will tell of his saving justice to a people yet unborn: he has fulfilled it.

23.1: [Psalm Of David] Yahweh is my shepherd, I lack nothing.
23.2: In grassy meadows he lets me lie. By tranquil streams he leads me
23.3: to restore my spirit. He guides me in paths of saving justice as befits his name.
23.4: Even were I to walk in a ravine as dark as death I should fear no danger, for you are at my side. Your staff and your crook are there to soothe me.
23.5: You prepare a table for me under the eyes of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup brims over.
23.6: Kindness and faithful love pursue me every day of my life. I make my home in the house of Yahweh for all time to come.

24.1: [Psalm Of David] To Yahweh belong the earth and all it contains, the world and all who live there;
24.2: it is he who laid its foundations on the seas, on the flowing waters fixed it firm.
24.3: Who shall go up to the mountain of Yahweh? Who shall take a stand in his holy place?
24.4: The clean of hands and pure of heart, whose heart is not set on vanities, who does not swear an oath in order to deceive.
24.5: Such a one will receive blessing from Yahweh, saving justice from the God of his salvation.
24.6: Such is the people that seeks him, that seeks your presence, God of Jacob.Pause
24.7: Gates, lift high your heads, raise high the ancient gateways, and the king of glory shall enter!
24.8: Who is he, this king of glory? It is Yahweh, strong and valiant, Yahweh valiant in battle.
24.9: Gates, lift high your heads, raise high the ancient gateways, and the king of glory shall enter!
24.10: Who is he, this king of glory? Yahweh Sabaoth, he is the king of glory.Pause

25.2: to you, my God. BUT in my trust in you do not put me to shame, let not my enemies gloat over me.
25.3: CALLING to you, none shall ever be put to shame, but shame is theirs who groundlessly break faith.
25.4: DIRECT me in your ways, Yahweh, and teach me your paths.
25.5: ENCOURAGE me to walk in your truth and teach me since you are the God who saves me. FOR my hope is in you all day long -- such is your generosity, Yahweh.
25.6: GOODNESS and faithful love have been yours for ever, Yahweh, do not forget them.
25.7: HOLD not my youthful sins against me, but remember me as your faithful love dictates.
25.8: INTEGRITY and generosity are marks of Yahweh for he brings sinners back to the path.
25.9: JUDICIOUSLY he guides the humble, instructing the poor in his way.
25.10: KINDNESS unfailing and constancy mark all Yahweh's paths, for those who keep his covenant and his decrees.
25.11: LET my sin, great though it is, be forgiven, Yahweh, for the sake of your name.
25.12: MEN who respect Yahweh, what of them? He teaches them the way they must choose.
25.13: NEIGHBOURS to happiness will they live, and their children inherit the land.
25.14: ONLY those who fear Yahweh have his secret and his covenant, for their understanding.
25.15: PERMANENTLY my eyes are on Yahweh, for he will free my feet from the snare.
25.16: QUICK, turn to me, pity me, alone and wretched as I am!
25.17: RELIEVE the distress of my heart, bring me out of my constraint.
25.18: SPARE a glance for my misery and pain, take all my sins away.
25.19: TAKE note how countless are my enemies, how violent their hatred for me.
25.20: UNLESS you guard me and rescue me I shall be put to shame, for you are my refuge.
25.21: VIRTUE and integrity be my protection, for my hope, Yahweh, is in you.
25.22: Ransom Israel, O God, from all its troubles.

26.1: [Of David] Yahweh, be my judge! I go on my way in innocence, my trust in Yahweh never wavers.
26.2: Probe me, Yahweh, examine me, Test my heart and my mind in the fire.
26.3: For your faithful love is before my eyes, and I live my life by your truth.
26.4: No sitting with wastrels for me, no travelling with hypocrites;
26.5: I hate the company of sinners, I refuse to sit down with the wicked.
26.6: I will wash my hands in innocence and join the procession round your altar, Yahweh,
26.7: to make heard the sound of thanksgiving, to proclaim all your wonders.
26.8: Yahweh, I love the beauty of your house and the place where your glory dwells.
26.9: Do not couple me with sinners, nor my life with men of violence,
26.10: whose hands are stained with guilt, their right hands heavy with bribes.
26.11: In innocence I will go on my way; ransom me, take pity on me.
26.12: I take my stand on the right path; I will bless you, Yahweh, in the assemblies.

27.1: [Of David] Yahweh is my light and my salvation, whom should I fear? Yahweh is the fortress of my life, whom should I dread?
27.2: When the wicked advance against me to eat me up, they, my opponents, my enemies, are the ones who stumble and fall.
27.3: Though an army pitch camp against me, my heart will not fear, though war break out against me, my trust will never be shaken.
27.4: One thing I ask of Yahweh, one thing I seek: to dwell in Yahweh's house all the days of my life, to enjoy the sweetness of Yahweh, to seek out his temple.
27.5: For he hides me away under his roof on the day of evil, he folds me in the recesses of his tent, sets me high on a rock.
27.6: Now my head is held high above the enemies who surround me; in his tent I will offer sacrifices of acclaim. I will sing, I will make music for Yahweh.
27.7: Yahweh, hear my voice as I cry, pity me, answer me!
27.8: Of you my heart has said, 'Seek his face!' Your face, Yahweh, I seek;
27.9: do not turn away from me. Do not thrust aside your servant in anger, without you I am helpless. Never leave me, never forsake me, God, my Saviour.
27.10: Though my father and mother forsake me, Yahweh will gather me up.
27.11: Yahweh, teach me your way, lead me on the path of integrity because of my enemies;
27.12: do not abandon me to the will of my foes -- false witnesses have risen against me, and are breathing out violence.
27.13: This I believe: I shall see the goodness of Yahweh, in the land of the living.
27.14: Put your hope in Yahweh, be strong, let your heart be bold, put your hope in Yahweh.

28.1: [Of David] To you, Yahweh, I cry, my rock, do not be deaf to me! If you stay silent I shall be like those who sink into oblivion.
28.2: Hear the sound of my prayer when I call upon you, when I raise my hands, Yahweh, towards your Holy of Holies.
28.3: Do not drag me away with the wicked, with evil-doers, who talk to their partners of peace with treachery in their hearts.
28.4: Repay them as their deeds deserve, as befits their treacherous actions; as befits their handiwork repay them, let their deserts fall back on themselves.
28.5: They do not comprehend the deeds of Yahweh, the work of his hands. May he pull them down and not rebuild them!
28.6: Blessed be Yahweh for he hears the sound of my prayer.
28.7: Yahweh is my strength and my shield, in him my heart trusts. I have been helped; my body has recovered its vigour, with all my heart I thank him.
28.8: Yahweh is the strength of his people, a safe refuge for his anointed.
28.9: Save your people, bless your heritage, shepherd them and carry them for ever!

29.1: [Psalm Of David] Give Yahweh his due, sons of God, give Yahweh his due of glory and strength,
29.2: give Yahweh the glory due to his name, adore Yahweh in the splendour of holiness.
29.3: Yahweh's voice over the waters, the God of glory thunders; Yahweh over countless waters,
29.4: Yahweh's voice in power, Yahweh's voice in splendour;
29.5: Yahweh's voice shatters cedars, Yahweh shatters cedars of Lebanon,
29.6: he makes Lebanon skip like a calf, Sirion like a young wild ox.
29.8: Yahweh's voice convulses the desert, Yahweh convulses the desert of Kadesh,
29.9: Yahweh's voice convulses terebinths, strips forests bare. In his palace all cry, 'Glory!'
29.10: Yahweh was enthroned for the flood, Yahweh is enthroned as king for ever.
29.11: Yahweh will give strength to his people, Yahweh blesses his people with peace.

30.1: [Psalm Canticle for the Dedication of the House Of David] I praise you to the heights, Yahweh, for you have raised me up, you have not let my foes make merry over me.
30.2: Yahweh, my God, I cried to you for help and you healed me.
30.3: Yahweh, you have lifted me out of Sheol, from among those who sink into oblivion you have given me life.
30.4: Make music for Yahweh, all you who are faithful to him, praise his unforgettable holiness.
30.5: His anger lasts but a moment, his favour through life; In the evening come tears, but with dawn cries of joy.
30.6: Carefree, I used to think, 'Nothing can ever shake me!'
30.7: Your favour, Yahweh, set me on impregnable heights, but you turned away your face and I was terrified.
30.8: To you, Yahweh, I call, to my God I cry for mercy.
30.9: What point is there in my death, my going down to the abyss? Can the dust praise you or proclaim your faithfulness?
30.10: Listen, Yahweh, take pity on me, Yahweh, be my help!
30.11: You have turned my mourning into dancing, you have stripped off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy.
30.12: So my heart will sing to you unceasingly, Yahweh, my God, I shall praise you for ever.

31.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] In you, Yahweh, I have taken refuge, let me never be put to shame, in your saving justice deliver me, rescue me,
31.2: turn your ear to me, make haste. Be for me a rock-fastness, a fortified citadel to save me.
31.3: You are my rock, my rampart; true to your name, lead me and guide me!
31.4: Draw me out of the net they have spread for me, for you are my refuge;
31.5: to your hands I commit my spirit, by you have I been redeemed. God of truth,
31.6: you hate those who serve useless idols; but my trust is in Yahweh:
31.7: I will delight and rejoice in your faithful love! You, who have seen my misery, and witnessed the miseries of my soul,
31.8: have not handed me over to the enemy, but have given me freedom to roam at large.
31.9: Take pity on me, Yahweh, for I am in trouble. Vexation is gnawing away my eyes, my soul deep within me.
31.10: For my life is worn out with sorrow, and my years with sighs. My strength gives way under my misery, and my bones are all wasted away.
31.11: The sheer number of my enemies makes me contemptible, loathsome to my neighbours, and my friends shrink from me in horror. When people see me in the street they take to their heels.
31.12: I have no more place in their hearts than a corpse, or something lost.
31.13: All I hear is slander -- terror wherever I turn -- as they plot together against me, scheming to take my life.
31.14: But my trust is in you, Yahweh; I say, 'You are my God,'
31.15: every moment of my life is in your hands, rescue me from the clutches of my foes who pursue me;
31.16: let your face shine on your servant, save me in your faithful love.
31.17: I call on you, Yahweh, so let disgrace fall not on me, but on the wicked. Let them go down to Sheol in silence,
31.18: muzzles on their lying mouths, which speak arrogantly against the upright in pride and contempt.
31.19: Yahweh, what quantities of good things you have in store for those who fear you, and bestow on those who make you their refuge, for all humanity to see.
31.20: Safe in your presence you hide them, far from human plotting, shielding them in your tent, far from contentious tongues.
31.21: Blessed be Yahweh who works for me miracles of his faithful love (in a fortified city)!
31.22: In a state of terror I cried, 'I have been cut off from your sight!' Yet you heard my plea for help when I cried out to you.
31.23: Love Yahweh, all his faithful: Yahweh protects his loyal servants, but he repays the arrogant with interest.
31.24: Be brave, take heart, all who put your hope in Yahweh.

32.1: [Of David Poem] How blessed are those whose offence is forgiven, whose sin blotted out.
32.2: How blessed are those to whom Yahweh imputes no guilt, whose spirit harbours no deceit.
32.3: I said not a word, but my bones wasted away from groaning all the day;
32.4: day and night your hand lay heavy upon me; my heart grew parched as stubble in summer drought.Pause
32.5: I made my sin known to you, did not conceal my guilt. I said, 'I shall confess my offence to Yahweh.' And you, for your part, took away my guilt, forgave my sin.Pause
32.6: That is why each of your faithful ones prays to you in time of distress. Even if great floods overflow, they will never reach your faithful.
32.7: You are a refuge for me, you guard me in trouble, with songs of deliverance you surround me.Pause
32.8: I shall instruct you and teach you the way to go; I shall not take my eyes off you.
32.9: Be not like a horse or a mule; that does not understand bridle or bit; if you advance to master them, there is no means of bringing them near.
32.10: Countless troubles are in store for the wicked, but one who trusts in Yahweh is enfolded in his faithful love.
32.11: Rejoice in Yahweh, exult all you upright, shout for joy, you honest of heart.

33.1: Shout for joy, you upright; praise comes well from the honest.
33.2: Give thanks to Yahweh on the lyre, play for him on the ten-stringed lyre.
33.3: Sing to him a new song, make sweet music for your cry of victory.
33.4: The word of Yahweh is straightforward, all he does springs from his constancy.
33.5: He loves uprightness and justice; the faithful love of Yahweh fills the earth.
33.6: By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, by the breath of his mouth all their array.
33.7: He collects the waters of the sea like a dam, he stores away the abyss in his treasure-house.
33.8: Let the whole earth fear Yahweh, let all who dwell in the world revere him;
33.9: for, the moment he spoke, it was so, no sooner had he commanded, than there it stood!
33.10: Yahweh thwarts the plans of nations, frustrates the counsels of peoples;
33.11: but Yahweh's own plan stands firm for ever, his heart's counsel from age to age.
33.12: How blessed the nation whose God is Yahweh, the people he has chosen as his heritage.
33.13: From heaven Yahweh looks down, he sees all the children of Adam,
33.14: from the place where he sits he watches all who dwell on the earth;
33.15: he alone moulds their hearts, he understands all they do.
33.16: A large army will not keep a king safe, nor his strength save a warrior's life;
33.17: it is delusion to rely on a horse for safety, for all its power it cannot save.
33.18: But see how Yahweh watches over those who fear him, those who rely on his faithful love,
33.19: to rescue them from death and keep them alive in famine.
33.20: We are waiting for Yahweh; he is our help and our shield,
33.21: for in him our heart rejoices, in his holy name we trust.
33.22: Yahweh, let your faithful love rest on us, as our hope has rested in you.

34.1: [Of David, when he had feigned insanity before Abimelech, and Abimelech sent him away] I will bless Yahweh at all times, his praise continually on my lips.
34.2: I will praise Yahweh from my heart; let the humble hear and rejoice.
34.3: Proclaim with me the greatness of Yahweh, let us acclaim his name together.
34.4: I seek Yahweh and he answers me, frees me from all my fears.
34.5: Fix your gaze on Yahweh and your face will grow bright, you will never hang your head in shame.
34.6: A pauper calls out and Yahweh hears, saves him from all his troubles.
34.7: The angel of Yahweh encamps around those who fear him, and rescues them.
34.8: Taste and see that Yahweh is good. How blessed are those who take refuge in him.
34.9: Fear Yahweh, you his holy ones; those who fear him lack for nothing.
34.10: Young lions may go needy and hungry, but those who seek Yahweh lack nothing good.
34.11: Come, my children, listen to me, I will teach you the fear of Yahweh.
34.12: Who among you delights in life, longs for time to enjoy prosperity?
34.13: Guard your tongue from evil, your lips from any breath of deceit.
34.14: Turn away from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it.
34.15: The eyes of Yahweh are on the upright, his ear turned to their cry.
34.16: But Yahweh's face is set against those who do evil, to cut off the memory of them from the earth.
34.17: They cry in anguish and Yahweh hears, and rescues them from all their troubles.
34.18: Yahweh is near to the broken-hearted, he helps those whose spirit is crushed.
34.19: Though hardships without number beset the upright, Yahweh brings rescue from them all.
34.20: Yahweh takes care of all their bones, not one of them will be broken.
34.21: But to the wicked evil brings death, those who hate the upright will pay the penalty.
34.22: Yahweh ransoms the lives of those who serve him, and there will be no penalty for those who take refuge in him.

35.1: [Of David] Accuse my accusers, Yahweh, attack my attackers.
35.2: Grasp your buckler and shield, up, and help me.
35.3: Brandish spear and pike to confront my pursuers, give me the assurance, 'I am your Saviour.'
35.4: Shame and humiliation on those who are out to kill me! Defeat and repulse in dismay on those who plot my downfall.
35.5: May they be like chaff before the wind, with the angel of Yahweh to chase them.
35.6: May their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of Yahweh to hound them.
35.7: Unprovoked they laid their snare for me, unprovoked dug a trap to kill me.
35.8: Ruin comes upon them unawares; the snare they have laid will catch them, and into their own trap they will fall.
35.9: Then I shall delight in Yahweh, rejoice that he has saved me.
35.10: My very bones will all exclaim, Yahweh, who can compare with you in rescuing the poor from the oppressor; the needy from the exploiter?
35.11: False witnesses come forward against me asking me questions I cannot answer, they cross-examine me,
35.12: repay my kindness with cruelty, make my life barren.
35.13: But I, when they were ill, had worn sackcloth, and mortified myself with fasting, praying ever anew in my heart,
35.14: as if for a friend or brother; I had wandered restless, as if mourning a mother, so bowed had I been in sorrow.
35.15: When I stumble they gather in glee, gather around me; strangers I never even knew tear me apart incessantly.
35.16: If I fall they surround me, grinding their teeth at me.
35.17: How much longer, Lord, will you look on? Rescue me from their onslaughts, from young lions rescue the one life that I have.
35.18: I will give you thanks in the great assembly praise you where the people gather.
35.19: Let not my lying enemies gloat over me; those who hate me unprovoked look askance at me.
35.20: They have no greeting of peace to the peace-loving people of the land; they think up deceptive speeches.
35.21: Their mouths wide open to accuse me, they say, 'Come on now, we saw you.'
35.22: You saw it, Yahweh, do not stay silent; Lord, do not stand aloof from me.
35.23: Up, awake, to my defence, my God and my Lord, to my cause.
35.24: In your saving justice give judgement for me, Yahweh my God, and do not let them gloat over me.
35.25: Do not let them think, 'Just as we hoped,' nor, 'Now we have swallowed him up.'
35.26: Shame and dismay on them all who gloat over my misfortunes. Let all who profit at my expense be covered with shame and disgrace.
35.27: But let all who delight in my uprightness shout for joy and gladness; let them constantly say, 'Great is Yahweh, who delights to see his servant in peace.'
35.28: And my tongue shall recount your saving justice, all day long sing your praise.

36.1: [For the choirmaster Of the servant of Yahweh Of David] Sin is the oracle of the wicked in the depths of his heart; there is no fear of God before his eyes.
36.2: He sees himself with too flattering an eye to detect and detest his guilt;
36.3: all he says is malicious and deceitful, he has turned his back on wisdom. To get his way
36.4: he hatches malicious plots even in his bed; once set on his evil course no wickedness is too much for him.
36.5: Yahweh, your faithful love is in the heavens, your constancy reaches to the clouds,
36.6: your saving justice is like towering mountains, your judgements like the mighty deep. Yahweh, you support both man and beast;
36.7: how precious, God, is your faithful love. So the children of Adam take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
36.8: They feast on the bounty of your house, you let them drink from your delicious streams;
36.9: in you is the source of life, by your light we see the light.
36.10: Maintain your faithful love to those who acknowledge you, and your saving justice to the honest of heart.
36.11: Do not let the foot of the arrogant overtake me or wicked hands drive me away.
36.12: There they have fallen, the evil-doers, flung down, never to rise again.

37.1: [Of David] Do not get heated about the wicked or envy those who do wrong.
37.2: Quick as the grass they wither, fading like the green of the fields.
37.3: Put your trust in Yahweh and do right, make your home in the land and live secure.
37.4: Make Yahweh your joy and he will give you your heart's desires.
37.5: Commit your destiny to Yahweh, be confident in him, and he will act,
37.6: making your uprightness clear as daylight, and the justice of your cause as the noon.
37.7: Stay quiet before Yahweh, wait longingly for him, do not get heated over someone who is making a fortune, succeeding by devious means.
37.8: Refrain from anger, leave rage aside, do not get heated -- it can do no good;
37.9: for evil-doers will be annihilated, while those who hope in Yahweh shall have the land for their own.
37.10: A little while and the wicked will be no more, however well you search for the place, the wicked will not be there;
37.11: but the poor will have the land for their own, to enjoy untroubled peace.
37.12: The wicked plots against the upright and gnashes his teeth at him,
37.13: but Yahweh only laughs at his efforts, knowing that his end is in sight.
37.14: Though the wicked draw his sword and bend his bow to slaughter the honest and bring down the poor and the needy,
37.15: his sword will pierce his own heart, and his bow will be shattered.
37.16: What little the upright possesses outweighs all the wealth of the wicked;
37.17: for the weapons of the wicked shall be shattered, while Yahweh supports the upright.
37.18: The lives of the just are in Yahweh's care, their birthright will endure for ever;
37.19: they will not be put to shame when bad times come, in time of famine they will have plenty.
37.20: The wicked, enemies of Yahweh, will be destroyed, they will vanish like the green of the pasture, they will vanish in smoke.
37.21: The wicked borrows and will not repay, but the upright is generous in giving;
37.22: those he blesses will have the land for their own, and those he curses be annihilated.
37.23: Yahweh guides a strong man's steps and keeps them firm; and takes pleasure in him.
37.24: When he trips he is not thrown sprawling, since Yahweh supports him by the hand.
37.25: Now I am old, but ever since my youth I never saw an upright person abandoned, or the descendants of the upright forced to beg their bread.
37.26: The upright is always compassionate, always lending, so his descendants reap a blessing.
37.27: Turn your back on evil and do good, you will have a home for ever,
37.28: for Yahweh loves justice and will not forsake his faithful. Evil-doers will perish eternally, the descendants of the wicked be annihilated,
37.29: but the upright shall have the land for their own, there they shall live for ever.
37.30: Wisdom comes from the lips of the upright, and his tongue speaks what is right;
37.31: the law of his God is in his heart, his foot will never slip.
37.32: The wicked keeps a close eye on the upright, looking out for a chance to kill him;
37.33: Yahweh will never abandon him to the clutches of the wicked, nor let him be condemned if he is tried.
37.34: Put your hope in Yahweh, keep to his path, he will raise you up to make the land your own; you will look on while the wicked are annihilated.
37.35: I have seen the wicked exultant, towering like a cedar of Lebanon.
37.36: When next I passed he was gone, I searched for him and he was nowhere to be found.
37.37: Observe the innocent, consider the honest, for the lover of peace will not lack children.
37.38: But the wicked will all be destroyed together, and their children annihilated.
37.39: The upright have Yahweh for their Saviour, their refuge in times of trouble;
37.40: Yahweh helps them and rescues them, he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them because they take refuge in him.

38.1: [Psalm Of David In commemoration] Yahweh, do not correct me in anger, do not discipline me in wrath.
38.2: For your arrows have pierced deep into me, your hand has pressed down upon me.
38.3: Your indignation has left no part of me unscathed, my sin has left no health in my bones.
38.4: My sins stand higher than my head, they weigh on me as an unbearable weight.
38.5: I have stinking, festering wounds, thanks to my folly.
38.6: I am twisted and bent double, I spend my days in gloom.
38.7: My loins burn with fever, no part of me is unscathed.
38.8: Numbed and utterly crushed I groan in distress of heart.
38.9: Lord, all my longing is known to you, my sighing no secret from you,
38.10: my heart is throbbing, my strength has failed, the light has gone out of my eyes.
38.11: Friends and companions shun my disease, even the dearest of them keep their distance.
38.12: Those with designs on my life lay snares, those who wish me ill speak of violence and hatch treachery all day long.
38.13: But I hear nothing, as though I were deaf, as though dumb, saying not a word.
38.14: I am like the one who, hearing nothing, has no sharp answer to make.
38.15: For in you, Yahweh, I put my hope, you, Lord my God, will give answer.
38.16: I said, 'Never let them gloat over me, do not let them take advantage of me if my foot slips.'
38.17: There is no escape for me from falling, no relief from my misery.
38.18: But I make no secret of my guilt, I am anxious at the thought of my sin.
38.19: There is no numbering those who oppose me without cause, no counting those who hate me unprovoked,
38.20: repaying me evil for good, slandering me for trying to do them good.
38.21: Yahweh, do not desert me, my God, do not stand aloof from me.
38.22: Come quickly to my help, Lord, my Saviour!

39.1: [For the choirmaster For Jeduthun Psalm Of David] I said, 'I will watch how I behave so that I do not sin by my tongue. I will keep a muzzle on my mouth as long as any sinner is near.'
39.2: I stayed dumb, silent, speechless, but the sinner's prosperity redoubled my torment.
39.3: My heart had been smouldering within me, but at the thought of this it flared up and the words came bursting out,
39.4: 'Yahweh, let me know my fate, how much longer I have to live. Show me just how frail I am.
39.5: 'Look, you have given me but a hand's breadth or two of life, the length of my life is as nothing to you. Every human being that stands on earth is a mere puff of wind,
39.6: every human being that walks only a shadow; a mere puff of wind is the wealth stored away -- no knowing who will profit from it.'
39.7: So now, Lord, what am I to hope for? My hope is in you.
39.8: Save me from all my sins, do not make me the butt of fools.
39.9: I keep silence, I speak no more since you yourself have been at work.
39.10: Take your scourge away from me. I am worn out by the blows you deal me.
39.11: You correct human beings by punishing sin, like a moth you eat away all their desires -- a human being is a mere puff of wind.
39.12: Yahweh, hear my prayer, listen to my cry for help, do not remain deaf to my weeping. For I am a stranger in your house, a nomad like all my ancestors.
39.13: Turn away your gaze that I may breathe freely before I depart and am no more!

40.1: [For the choirmaster Of David Psalm] I waited, I waited for Yahweh, then he stooped to me and heard my cry for help.
40.2: He pulled me up from the seething chasm, from the mud of the mire. He set my feet on rock, and made my footsteps firm.
40.3: He put a fresh song in my mouth, praise of our God. Many will be awestruck at the sight, and will put their trust in Yahweh.
40.4: How blessed are those who put their trust in Yahweh, who have not sided with rebels and those who have gone astray in falsehood.
40.5: How much you have done, Yahweh, my God -- your wonders, your plans for us -- you have no equal. I will proclaim and speak of them; they are beyond number.
40.6: You wanted no sacrifice or cereal offering, but you gave me an open ear, you did not ask for burnt offering or sacrifice for sin;
40.7: then I said, 'Here I am, I am coming.' In the scroll of the book it is written of me,
40.8: my delight is to do your will; your law, my God, is deep in my heart.
40.9: I proclaimed the saving justice of Yahweh in the great assembly. See, I will not hold my tongue, as you well know.
40.10: I have not kept your saving justice locked in the depths of my heart, but have spoken of your constancy and saving help. I have made no secret of your faithful and steadfast love, in the great assembly.
40.11: You, Yahweh, have not withheld your tenderness from me; your faithful and steadfast love will always guard me.
40.12: For troubles surround me, until they are beyond number; my sins have overtaken me; I cannot see my way. They outnumber the hairs of my head, and my heart fails me.
40.13: Be pleased, Yahweh, to rescue me, Yahweh, come quickly and help me!
40.14: Shame and dismay to all who seek to take my life. Back with them, let them be humiliated who delight in my misfortunes.
40.15: Let them be aghast with shame, those who say to me, 'Aha, aha!'
40.16: But joy and happiness in you to all who seek you! Let them ceaselessly cry, 'Great is Yahweh' who love your saving power.
40.17: Poor and needy as I am, the Lord has me in mind. You, my helper, my Saviour, my God, do not delay.

41.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] Blessed is anyone who cares for the poor and the weak; in time of trouble Yahweh rescues him.
41.2: Yahweh protects him, gives him life and happiness on earth. Do not abandon him to his enemies' pleasure!
41.3: Yahweh sustains him on his bed of sickness; you transform altogether the bed where he lies sick.
41.4: For my part I said, 'Yahweh, take pity on me! Cure me for I have sinned against you.'
41.5: My enemies speak to me only of disaster, 'When will he die and his name disappear?'
41.6: When people come to see me their talk is hollow, when they get out they spread the news with spite in their hearts.
41.7: All who hate me whisper together about me and reckon I deserve the misery I suffer.
41.8: 'A fatal sickness has a grip on him; now that he is down, he will never get up again.'
41.9: Even my trusted friend on whom I relied, who shared my table, takes advantage of me.
41.10: But you, Yahweh, take pity on me! Put me on my feet and I will give them their due.
41.11: This will convince me that you delight in me, if my enemy no longer exults over me.
41.12: Then you will keep me unscathed, and set me in your presence for ever.
41.13: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from eternity to eternity. Amen, Amen.

42.1: [For the choirmaster Poem Of the sons of Korah] As a deer yearns for running streams, so I yearn for you, my God.
42.2: I thirst for God, the living God; when shall I go to see the face of God?
42.3: I have no food but tears day and night, as all day long I am taunted, 'Where is your God?'
42.4: This I remember as I pour out my heart, how I used to pass under the roof of the Most High used to go to the house of God, among cries of joy and praise, the sound of the feast.
42.5: Why be so downcast, why all these sighs? Hope in God! I will praise him still, my Saviour,
42.6: my God. When I am downcast I think of you: from the land of Jordan and Hermon, I think of you, humble mountain.
42.7: Deep is calling to deep by the roar of your cataracts, all your waves and breakers have rolled over me.
42.8: In the daytime God sends his faithful love, and even at night; the song it inspires in me is a prayer to my living God.
42.9: I shall say to God, my rock, 'Why have you forgotten me? Why must I go around in mourning, harrassed by the enemy?'
42.10: With death in my bones, my enemies taunt me, all day long they ask me, 'Where is your God?'
42.11: Why so downcast, why all these sighs? Hope in God! I will praise him still, my Saviour, my God.

43.1: Judge me, God, defend my cause against a people who have no faithful love; from those who are treacherous and unjust, rescue me.
43.2: For you are the God of my strength; why abandon me? Why must I go around in mourning, harrassed by the enemy?
43.3: Send out your light and your truth; they shall be my guide, to lead me to your holy mountain to the place where you dwell.
43.4: Then I shall go to the altar of God, to the God of my joy. I will rejoice and praise you on the harp, O God, my God.
43.5: Why so downcast, why all these sighs? Hope in God! I will praise him still, my Saviour, my God.

44.1: [For the choirmaster Of the sons of Korah Poem] God, we have heard for ourselves, our ancestors have told us, of the deeds you did in their days, in days of old,
44.2: by your hand. To establish them in the land you drove out nations, to make room for them you harried peoples.
44.3: It was not their own sword that won the land, nor their own arms which made them victorious, but your hand it was and your arm, and the light of your presence, for you loved them.
44.4: You are my king, my God, who decreed Jacob's victories;
44.5: through you we conquered our opponents, in your name we trampled down those who rose up against us.
44.6: For my trust was not in my bow, my victory was not won by my sword;
44.7: it was you who saved us from our opponents, you who put to shame those who hate us.
44.8: Our boast was always of God, we praised your name without ceasing.Pause
44.9: Yet now you have abandoned and humiliated us, you no longer take the field with our armies,
44.10: you leave us to fall back before the enemy, those who hate us plunder us at will.
44.11: You hand us over like sheep for slaughter, you scatter us among the nations,
44.12: you sell your people for a trifle and make no profit on the sale.
44.13: You make us the butt of our neighbours, the mockery and scorn of those around us,
44.14: you make us a by-word among nations, other peoples shake their heads over us.
44.15: All day long I brood on my disgrace, the shame written clear on my face,
44.16: from the sound of insult and abuse, from the sight of hatred and vengefulness.
44.17: All this has befallen us though we had not forgotten you, nor been disloyal to your covenant,
44.18: our hearts never turning away, our feet never straying from your path.
44.19: Yet you have crushed us in the place where jackals live, and immersed us in shadow dark as death.
44.20: Had we forgotten the name of our God and stretched out our hands to a foreign god,
44.21: would not God have found this out, for he knows the secrets of the heart?
44.22: For your sake we are being massacred all day long, treated as sheep to be slaughtered.
44.23: Wake, Lord! Why are you asleep? Awake! Do not abandon us for good.
44.24: Why do you turn your face away, forgetting that we are poor and harrassed?
44.25: For we are bowed down to the dust, and lie prone on the ground.
44.26: Arise! Come to our help! Ransom us, as your faithful love demands.

45.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'Lilies . . .' Of the sons of Korah Poem Love song] My heart is stirred by a noble theme, I address my poem to the king, my tongue the pen of an expert scribe.
45.2: Of all men you are the most handsome, gracefulness is a dew upon your lips, for God has blessed you for ever.
45.3: Warrior, strap your sword at your side, in your majesty and splendour advance,
45.4: ride on in the cause of truth, gentleness and uprightness. Stretch the bowstring tight, lending terror to your right hand.
45.5: Your arrows are sharp, nations lie at your mercy, the king's enemies lose heart.
45.6: Your throne is from God, for ever and ever, the sceptre of your kingship a sceptre of justice,
45.7: you love uprightness and detest evil. This is why God, your God, has anointed you with oil of gladness, as none of your rivals,
45.8: your robes all myrrh and aloes. From palaces of ivory, harps bring you joy,
45.9: in your retinue are daughters of kings, the consort at your right hand in gold of Ophir.
45.10: Listen, my daughter, attend to my words and hear; forget your own nation and your ancestral home,
45.11: then the king will fall in love with your beauty; he is your lord, bow down before him.
45.12: The daughter of Tyre will court your favour with gifts, and the richest of peoples
45.13: with jewels set in gold. Clothed
45.14: in brocade, the king's daughter is led within to the king with the maidens of her retinue; her companions are brought to her,
45.15: they enter the king's palace with joy and rejoicing.
45.16: Instead of your ancestors you will have sons; you will make them rulers over the whole world.
45.17: I will make your name endure from generation to generation, so nations will sing your praise for ever and ever.

46.1: [For the choirmaster Of the sons of Korah For oboe Song] God is both refuge and strength for us, a help always ready in trouble;
46.2: so we shall not be afraid though the earth be in turmoil, though mountains tumble into the depths of the sea,
46.3: and its waters roar and seethe, and the mountains totter as it heaves. (Yahweh Sabaoth is with us, our citadel, the God of Jacob.)Pause
46.4: There is a river whose streams bring joy to God's city, it sanctifies the dwelling of the Most High.
46.5: God is in the city, it cannot fall; at break of day God comes to its rescue.
46.6: Nations are in uproar, kingdoms are tumbling, when he raises his voice the earth crumbles away.
46.7: Yahweh Sabaoth is with us, our citadel, the God of Jacob. Pause
46.8: Come, consider the wonders of Yahweh, the astounding deeds he has done on the earth;
46.9: he puts an end to wars over the whole wide world, he breaks the bow, he snaps the spear, shields he burns in the fire.
46.10: 'Be still and acknowledge that I am God, supreme over nations, supreme over the world.'
46.11: Yahweh Sabaoth is with us, our citadel, the God of Jacob.Pause

47.1: [For the choirmaster Of the sons of Korah Psalm] Clap your hands, all peoples, acclaim God with shouts of joy.
47.2: For Yahweh, the Most High, is glorious, the great king over all the earth.
47.3: He brings peoples under our yoke and nations under our feet.
47.4: He chooses for us our birthright, the pride of Jacob whom he loves.Pause
47.5: God goes up to shouts of acclaim, Yahweh to a fanfare on the ram's horn.
47.6: Let the music sound for our God, let it sound, let the music sound for our king, let it sound.
47.7: For he is king of the whole world; learn the music, let it sound for God!
47.8: God reigns over the nations, seated on his holy throne.
47.9: The leaders of the nations rally to the people of the God of Abraham. The shields of the earth belong to God, who is exalted on high.

48.1: [Song Psalm Of the sons of Korah] Great is Yahweh and most worthy of praise in the city of our God, the holy mountain,
48.2: towering in beauty, the joy of the whole world: Mount Zion in the heart of the north, the settlement of the great king;
48.3: God himself among its palaces has proved himself its bulwark.
48.4: For look, kings made alliance, together they advanced;
48.5: without a second glance, when they saw, they panicked and fled away.
48.6: Trembling seized them on the spot, pains like those of a woman in labour;
48.7: it was the east wind, that wrecker of ships from Tarshish.
48.8: What we had heard we saw for ourselves in the city of our God, in the city of Yahweh Sabaoth, which God has established for ever.Pause
48.9: We reflect on your faithful love, God, in your temple!
48.10: Both your name and your praise, God, are over the whole wide world. Your right hand is full of saving justice,
48.11: Mount Zion rejoices, the daughters of Judah delight because of your saving justice.
48.12: Go round Zion, walk right through her, count her bastions,
48.13: admire her walls, examine her palaces, to tell future generations
48.14: that such is God; our God for ever and ever, he is our guide!

49.1: [For the choirmaster Of the sons of Korah Psalm] Hear this, all nations, listen, all who dwell on earth,
49.2: people high and low, rich and poor alike!
49.3: My lips have wisdom to utter, my heart good sense to whisper.
49.4: I listen carefully to a proverb, I set my riddle to the music of the harp.
49.5: Why should I be afraid in times of trouble? Malice dogs me and hems me in.
49.6: They trust in their wealth, and boast of the profusion of their riches.
49.7: But no one can ever redeem himself or pay his own ransom to God,
49.8: the price for himself is too high; it can never be
49.9: that he will live on for ever and avoid the sight of the abyss.
49.10: For he will see the wise also die no less than the fool and the brute, and leave their wealth behind for others.
49.11: For ever no home but their tombs, their dwelling-place age after age, though they gave their name to whole territories.
49.12: In prosperity people lose their good sense, they become no better than dumb animals.
49.13: So they go on in their self-assurance, right up to the end they are content with their lot.Pause
49.14: They are penned in Sheol like sheep, Death will lead them to pasture, and those who are honest will rule over them. In the morning all trace of them will be gone, Sheol will be their home.
49.15: But my soul God will ransom from the clutches of Sheol, and will snatch me up.Pause
49.16: Do not be overawed when someone gets rich, and lives in ever greater splendour;
49.17: when he dies he will take nothing with him, his wealth will not go down with him.
49.18: Though he pampered himself while he lived -- and people praise you for looking after yourself-
49.19: he will go to join the ranks of his ancestors, who will never again see the light.
49.20: In prosperity people lose their good sense, they become no better than dumb animals.

50.1: [Psalm Of Asaph] The God of gods, Yahweh, is speaking, from east to west he summons the earth.
50.2: From Zion, perfection of beauty, he shines forth;
50.3: he is coming, our God, and will not be silent. Devouring fire ahead of him, raging tempest around him,
50.4: he summons the heavens from on high, and the earth to judge his people.
50.5: 'Gather to me my faithful, who sealed my covenant by sacrifice.'
50.6: The heavens proclaim his saving justice, 'God himself is judge.'Pause
50.7: 'Listen, my people, I am speaking, Israel, I am giving evidence against you, I, God, your God.
50.8: 'It is not with your sacrifices that I find fault, those burnt offerings constantly before me;
50.9: I will not accept any bull from your homes, nor a single goat from your folds.
50.10: 'For all forest creatures are mine already, the animals on the mountains in their thousands.
50.11: I know every bird in the air, whatever moves in the fields is mine.
