50.12: 'If I am hungry I shall not tell you, since the world and all it holds is mine.
50.13: Am I to eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
50.14: 'Let thanksgiving be your sacrifice to God, fulfil the vows you make to the Most High;
50.15: then if you call to me in time of trouble I will rescue you and you will honour me.'
50.16: But to the wicked, God says: 'What right have you to recite my statutes, to take my covenant on your lips,
50.17: when you detest my teaching, and thrust my words behind you?
50.18: 'You make friends with a thief as soon as you see one, you feel at home with adulterers,
50.19: your conversation is devoted to wickedness, and your tongue to inventing lies.
50.20: 'You sit there, slandering your own brother, you malign your own mother's son.
50.21: You do this, and am I to say nothing? Do you think that I am really like you? I charge you, indict you to your face.
50.22: 'Think it out, you who forget God, or I will tear you apart without hope of a rescuer.
50.23: Honour to me is a sacrifice of thanksgiving; to the upright I will show God's salvation.'

51.1: [For the choirmaster Of David When the prophet Nathan had come to him because he had gone to Bathsheba] Have mercy on me, O God, in your faithful love, in your great tenderness wipe away my offences;
51.2: wash me clean from my guilt, purify me from my sin.
51.3: For I am well aware of my offences, my sin is constantly in mind.
51.4: Against you, you alone, I have sinned, I have done what you see to be wrong, that you may show your saving justice when you pass sentence, and your victory may appear when you give judgement,
51.5: remember, I was born guilty, a sinner from the moment of conception.
51.6: But you delight in sincerity of heart, and in secret you teach me wisdom.
51.7: Purify me with hyssop till I am clean, wash me till I am whiter than snow.
51.8: Let me hear the sound of joy and gladness, and the bones you have crushed will dance.
51.9: Turn away your face from my sins, and wipe away all my guilt.
51.10: God, create in me a clean heart, renew within me a resolute spirit,
51.11: do not thrust me away from your presence, do not take away from me your spirit of holiness.
51.12: Give me back the joy of your salvation, sustain in me a generous spirit.
51.13: I shall teach the wicked your paths, and sinners will return to you.
51.14: Deliver me from bloodshed, God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will acclaim your saving justice.
51.15: Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will speak out your praise.
51.16: Sacrifice gives you no pleasure, burnt offering you do not desire.
51.17: Sacrifice to God is a broken spirit, a broken, contrite heart you never scorn.
51.18: In your graciousness do good to Zion, rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
51.19: Then you will delight in upright sacrifices,-burnt offerings and whole oblations -- and young bulls will be offered on your altar.

52.1: [For the choirmaster Poem Of David When Doeg the Edomite went and warned Saul, 'David has gone to Abimelech's house'] Why take pride in being wicked, you champion in villainy, all day long
52.2: plotting crime? Your tongue is razor-sharp, you artist in perfidy.
52.3: You prefer evil to good, lying to uprightness. Pause
52.4: You revel in destructive talk, treacherous tongue!
52.5: That is why God will crush you, destroy you once and for all, snatch you from your tent, uproot you from the land of the living.Pause
52.6: The upright will be awestruck as they see it, they will mock him,
52.7: 'So much for someone who would not place his reliance in God, but relied on his own great wealth, and made himself strong by crime.'
52.8: But I, like a flourishing olive tree in the house of God, put my trust in God's faithful love, for ever and ever.
52.9: I shall praise you for ever for what you have done, and shall trust in your name, so full of goodness, in the presence of your faithful.

53.1: [For the choirmaster In sickness Poem Of David] The fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God!' They are corrupt, vile and unjust, not one of them does right.
53.2: God looks down from heaven at the children of Adam, to see if a single one is wise, a single one seeks God.
53.3: All have proved faithless, all alike turned sour, not one of them does right, not a single one.
53.4: Are they not aware, these evil-doers? They are devouring my people; this is the bread they eat, and they never call upon God.
53.5: They will be gripped with fear, just where there is no need for fear, for God scatters the bones of him who besieges you; they are mocked because God rejects them.
53.6: Who will bring from Zion salvation for Israel? When God brings his people home, what joy for Jacob, what happiness for Israel!

54.1: [For the choirmaster On stringed instruments Poem Of David When the Ziphites went to Saul and said,'Is not David hiding with us?'] God, save me by your name, in your power vindicate me.
54.2: God, hear my prayer, listen to the words I speak.
54.3: Arrogant men are attacking me, bullies hounding me to death, no room in their thoughts for God.Pause
54.4: But now God is coming to my help, the Lord, among those who sustain me.
54.5: May their wickedness recoil on those who lie in wait for me. Yahweh, in your constancy destroy them.
54.6: How gladly will I offer you sacrifice, and praise your name, for it is good,
54.7: for it has rescued me from all my troubles, and my eye has feasted on my enemies.

55.1: [For the choirmaster For strings Poem Of David] God, hear my prayer, do not hide away from my plea,
55.2: give me a hearing, answer me, my troubles give me no peace. I shudder
55.3: at the enemy's shouts, at the outcry of the wicked; they heap up charges against me, in their anger bring hostile accusations against me.
55.4: My heart writhes within me, the terrors of death come upon me,
55.5: fear and trembling overwhelm me, and shuddering grips me.
55.6: And I say, 'Who will give me wings like a dove, to fly away and find rest?'
55.7: How far I would escape, and make a nest in the desert!Pause
55.8: I would soon find a refuge from the storm of abuse, from the
55.9: destructive tempest, Lord, from the flood of their tongues. For I see violence and strife in the city,
55.10: day and night they make their rounds along the city walls, Inside live malice and mischief,
55.11: inside lives destruction, tyranny and treachery never absent from its central square.
55.12: Were it an enemy who insulted me, that I could bear; if an opponent pitted himself against me, I could turn away from him.
55.13: But you, a person of my own rank, a comrade and dear friend,
55.14: to whom I was bound by intimate friendship in the house of God! May they recoil in disorder,
55.15: may death descend on them, may they go down alive to Sheol, since evil shares their home with them.
55.16: For my part, I appeal to God, and Yahweh saves me;
55.17: evening, morning, noon, I complain and I groan. He hears my cry,
55.18: he ransoms me and gives me peace from the feud against me, for they are taking me to law.
55.19: But God will listen and will humble them, he who has been enthroned from the beginning; no change of heart for them, for they do not fear God.
55.20: They attack those at peace with them, going back on their oaths;
55.21: though their mouth is smoother than butter, enmity is in their hearts; their words more soothing than oil, yet sharpened like swords.
55.22: Unload your burden onto Yahweh and he will sustain you; never will he allow the upright to stumble.
55.23: You, God, will thrust them down to the abyss of destruction, men bloodthirsty and deceptive, before half their days are spent. For my part, I put my trust in you.

56.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'The oppression of distant princes' Of David In a quiet voice When the Philistines seized him in Gath] Take pity on me, God, as they harry me, pressing their attacks home all day.
56.2: Those who harry me lie in wait for me all day, countless are those who attack me from the heights.
56.3: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you,
56.4: in God, whose word I praise, in God I put my trust and have no fear, what power has human strength over me?
56.5: All day long they carp at my words, their only thought is to harm me,
56.6: they gather together, lie in wait and spy on my movements, as though determined to take my life.
56.7: Because of this crime reject them, in your anger, God, strike down the nations.
56.8: You yourself have counted up my sorrows, collect my tears in your wineskin.
56.9: Then my enemies will turn back on the day when I call. This I know, that God is on my side.
56.10: In God whose word I praise, in Yahweh whose word I praise,
56.11: in God I put my trust and have no fear; what can mortal man do to me?
56.12: I am bound by the vows I have made, God, I will pay you the debt of thanks,
56.13: for you have saved my life from death to walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.

57.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'Do not destroy' Of David In a quiet voice When he escaped from Saul in the cave] Take pity on me, God, take pity on me, for in you I take refuge, in the shadow of your wings I take refuge, until the destruction is past.
57.2: I call to God the Most High, to God who has done everything for me;
57.3: may he send from heaven and save me, and check those who harry me;Pause may God send his faithful love and his constancy.
57.4: I lie surrounded by lions, greedy for human prey, their teeth are spears and arrows, their tongue a sharp sword.
57.5: Be exalted above the heavens, God! Your glory over all the earth!
57.6: They laid a snare in my path -- I was bowed with care -- they dug a pit ahead of me, but fell in it themselves.Pause
57.7: My heart is ready, God, my heart is ready; I will sing, and make music for you.
57.8: Awake, my glory, awake, lyre and harp, that I may awake the Dawn.
57.9: I will praise you among the peoples, Lord, I will make music for you among nations,
57.10: for your faithful love towers to heaven, your constancy to the clouds.
57.11: Be exalted above the heavens, God! Your glory over all the earth!

58.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'Do not destroy' Of David In a quiet voice] Divine as you are, do you truly give upright verdicts? do you judge fairly the children of Adam?
58.2: No! You devise injustice in your hearts, and with your hands you administer tyranny on the earth.
58.3: Since the womb they have gone astray, the wicked, on the wrong path since their birth, with their unjust verdicts.
58.4: They are poisonous as any snake, deaf as an adder that blocks its ears
58.5: so as not to hear the magician's music, however skilful his spells.
58.6: God, break the teeth in their mouths, snap off the fangs of these young lions, Yahweh.
58.7: May they drain away like water running to waste, may they wither like trampled grass,
58.8: like the slug that melts as it moves or a still-born child that never sees the sun.
58.9: Before they sprout thorns like the bramble, green or burnt up, may retribution whirl them away.
58.10: The upright will rejoice to see vengeance done, and will bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: 'So', people will say, 'the upright does have a reward; there is a God to dispense justice on earth.'

59.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'Do not destroy' Of David In a quiet voice When Saul sent men to watch David's house in order to have him killed] Rescue me from my enemies, my God, be my stronghold from my assailants,
59.2: rescue me from evil-doers, from men of violence save me.
59.3: Look at them, lurking to ambush me, violent men are attacking me, for no fault, no sin of mine, Yahweh,
59.4: for no guilt, they come running to take up position. Wake up, stand by me and keep watch,
59.5: Yahweh, God of Sabaoth, God of Israel, rise up, to punish all the nations, show no mercy to all these malicious traitors.Pause
59.6: Back they come at nightfall, snarling like curs, prowling through the town.
59.7: Look how they rant in speech with swords on their lips, 'Who is there to hear us?'
59.8: For your part, Yahweh, you laugh at them, you make mockery of all nations.
59.9: My strength, I keep my eyes fixed on you. For my stronghold is God,
59.10: the God who loves me faithfully is coming to meet me, God will let me feast my eyes on those who lie in wait for me.
59.11: Do not annihilate them, or my people may forget; shake them in your power, bring them low, Lord, our shield.
59.12: Sin is in their mouths, sin on their lips, so let them be trapped in their pride for the curses and lies that they utter.
59.13: Destroy them in your anger, destroy them till they are no more, and let it be known that God is Master in Jacob and the whole wide world.Pause
59.14: Back they come at nightfall, snarling like curs, prowling through the town,
59.15: scavenging for something to eat, growling unless they have their fill.
59.16: And so I will sing of your strength, in the morning acclaim your faithful love; you have been a stronghold for me, a refuge when I was in trouble.
59.17: My strength, I will make music for you, for my stronghold is God, the God who loves me faithfully.

60.1: [For the choirmaster To the tune 'The decree is a lily' In a quiet voice Of David To be learnt When he was at war with Aram-Naharaim and Aram-Zobah, and Joab marched back to destroy twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt] God, you have rejected us, broken us, you were angry, come back to us!
60.2: You made the earth tremble, split it open; now mend the rifts, it is tottering still.
60.3: You have forced your people to drink a bitter draught, forced us to drink a wine that made us reel.
60.4: You gave a signal to those who fear you to let them escape out of range of the bow.Pause
60.5: To rescue those you love, save with your right hand and answer us.
60.6: God has spoken from his sanctuary, 'In triumph I will divide up Shechem, and share out the Valley of Succoth.
60.7: 'Mine is Gilead, mine Manasseh, Ephraim the helmet on my head, Judah my commander's baton,
60.8: 'Moab a bowl for me to wash in, on Edom I plant my sandal. Now try shouting "Victory!" over me, Philistia!'
60.9: Who will lead me against a fortified city, who will guide me into Edom,
60.10: if not you, the God who has rejected us? God, you no longer march with our armies.
60.11: Bring us help in our time of crisis, any human help is worthless.
60.12: With God we shall do deeds of valour, he will trample down our enemies.

61.1: [For the choirmaster For strings Of David] God, hear my cry, listen to my prayer.
61.2: From the end of the earth I call to you with fainting heart. Lead me to the high rock that stands far out of my reach.
61.3: For you are my refuge, a strong tower against the enemy.
61.4: Let me stay in your tent for ever, taking refuge in the shelter of your wings!
61.5: For you, God, accept my vows, you grant me the heritage of those who fear your name.
61.6: Let the king live on and on, let his years continue age after age.
61.7: May his throne be always in God's presence, your faithful love and constancy watch over him.
61.8: Then I shall always sing to your name, day after day fulfilling my vows.

62.1: [For the choirmaster . . . Jeduthun Psalm Of David] In God alone there is rest for my soul, from him comes my safety;
62.2: he alone is my rock, my safety, my stronghold so that I stand unshaken.
62.3: How much longer will you set on a victim, all together, intent on murder, like a rampart already leaning over, a wall already damaged?
62.4: Trickery is their only plan, deception their only pleasure, with lies on their lips they pronounce a blessing, with a curse in their hearts.Pause
62.5: Rest in God alone, my soul! He is the source of my hope.
62.6: He alone is my rock, my safety, my stronghold, so that I stand unwavering.
62.7: In God is my safety and my glory, the rock of my strength. In God is my refuge;
62.8: trust in him, you people, at all times. Pour out your hearts to him, God is a refuge for us.Pause
62.9: Ordinary people are a mere puff of wind, important people a delusion; set both on the scales together, and they are lighter than a puff of wind.
62.10: Put no trust in extortion, no empty hopes in robbery; however much wealth may multiply, do not set your heart on it.
62.11: Once God has spoken, twice have I heard this: Strength belongs to God,
62.12: to you, Lord, faithful love; and you repay everyone as their deeds deserve.

63.1: [Psalm Of David When he was in the desert of Judah] God, you are my God, I pine for you; my heart thirsts for you, my body longs for you, as a land parched, dreary and waterless.
63.2: Thus I have gazed on you in the sanctuary, seeing your power and your glory.
63.3: Better your faithful love than life itself; my lips will praise you.
63.4: Thus I will bless you all my life, in your name lift up my hands.
63.5: All my longings fulfilled as with fat and rich foods, a song of joy on my lips and praise in my mouth.
63.6: On my bed when I think of you, I muse on you in the watches of the night,
63.7: for you have always been my help; in the shadow of your wings I rejoice;
63.8: my heart clings to you, your right hand supports me.
63.9: May those who are hounding me to death go down to the depths of the earth,
63.10: given over to the blade of the sword, and left as food for jackals.
63.11: Then the king shall rejoice in God, all who swear by him shall gain recognition, for the mouths of liars shall be silenced.

64.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David] Listen, God, to my voice as I plead, protect my life from fear of the enemy;
64.2: hide me from the league of the wicked, from the gang of evil-doers.
64.3: They sharpen their tongues like a sword, aim their arrows of poisonous abuse,
64.4: shoot at the innocent from cover, shoot suddenly, with nothing to fear.
64.5: They support each other in their evil designs, they discuss how to lay their snares. 'Who will see us?' they say,
64.6: 'or will penetrate our secrets?' He will do that, he who penetrates human nature to its depths, the depths of the heart.
64.7: God has shot them with his arrow, sudden were their wounds.
64.8: He brings them down because of their tongue, and all who see them shake their heads.
64.9: Everyone will be awestruck, proclaim what God has done, and understand why he has done it.
64.10: The upright will rejoice in Yahweh, will take refuge in him, and all the honest will praise him.

65.1: [For the choirmaster Psalm Of David Song] Praise is rightfully yours, God, in Zion. Vows to you shall be fulfilled,
65.2: for you answer prayer. All humanity must come to you
65.3: with its sinful deeds. Our faults overwhelm us, but you blot them out.
65.4: How blessed those whom you choose and invite to dwell in your courts. We shall be filled with the good things of your house, of your holy temple.
65.5: You respond to us with the marvels of your saving justice, God our Saviour, hope of the whole wide world, even the distant islands.
65.6: By your strength you hold the mountains steady, being clothed in power,
65.7: you calm the turmoil of the seas, the turmoil of their waves. The nations are in uproar, in panic those who live at the ends of the earth;
65.8: your miracles bring shouts of joy to the gateways of morning and evening.
65.9: You visit the earth and make it fruitful, you fill it with riches; the river of God brims over with water, you provide the grain. To that end
65.10: you water its furrows abundantly, level its ridges, soften it with showers and bless its shoots.
65.11: You crown the year with your generosity, richness seeps from your tracks,
65.12: the pastures of the desert grow moist, the hillsides are wrapped in joy,
65.13: the meadows are covered with flocks, the valleys clothed with wheat; they shout and sing for joy.

66.1: [For the choirmaster Song Psalm] Acclaim God, all the earth,
66.2: sing psalms to the glory of his name, glorify him with your praises,
66.3: say to God, 'How awesome you are! 'Your achievements are the measure of your power, your enemies woo your favour,
66.4: all the earth bows down before you, sings psalms to you, sings psalms to your name.'Pause
66.5: Come and see the marvels of God, his awesome deeds for the children of Adam:
66.6: he changed the sea into dry land, they crossed the river on foot. So let us rejoice in him,
66.7: who rules for ever by his power; his eyes keep watch on the nations to forestall rebellion against him.Pause
66.8: Nations, bless our God, let the sound of his praise be heard;
66.9: he brings us to life and keeps our feet from stumbling.
66.10: God, you have put us to the test, refined us like silver,
66.11: let us fall into the net; you have put a heavy strain on our backs,
66.12: let men ride over our heads; but now the ordeal by fire and water is over, you have led us out to breathe again.
66.13: I bring burnt offerings to your house, I fulfil to you my vows,
66.14: the vows that rose to my lips, that I pronounced when I was in trouble.
66.15: I will offer you rich burnt offerings, with the smoke of burning rams. I will sacrifice to you bullocks and goats.Pause
66.16: Come and listen, all who fear God, while I tell what he has done for me.
66.17: To him I cried aloud, high praise was on my tongue.
66.18: Had I been aware of guilt in my heart, the Lord would not have listened,
66.19: but in fact God did listen, attentive to the sound of my prayer.
66.20: Blessed be God who has not turned away my prayer, nor his own faithful love from me.

67.1: [For the choirmaster For strings Psalm Song] May God show kindness and bless us, and make his face shine on us.Pause
67.2: Then the earth will acknowledge your ways, and all nations your power to save.
67.3: Let the nations praise you, God, let all the nations praise you.
67.4: Let the nations rejoice and sing for joy, for you judge the world with justice, you judge the peoples with fairness, you guide the nations on earth.Pause
67.5: Let the nations praise you, God, let all the nations praise you.
67.6: The earth has yielded its produce; God, our God has blessed us.
67.7: May God continue to bless us, and be revered by the whole wide world.

68.1: [For the choirmaster Of David Psalm Song] Let God arise, let his enemies scatter, let his opponents flee before him.
68.2: You disperse them like smoke; as wax melts in the presence of a fire, so the wicked melt at the presence of God.
68.3: The upright rejoice in the presence of God, delighted and crying out for joy.
68.4: Sing to God, play music to his name, build a road for the Rider of the Clouds, rejoice in Yahweh, dance before him.
68.5: Father of orphans, defender of widows, such is God in his holy dwelling.
68.6: God gives the lonely a home to live in, leads prisoners out into prosperity, but rebels must live in the bare wastelands.
68.7: God, when you set out at the head of your people, when you strode over the desert,
68.8: the earth rocked,Pause the heavens pelted down rain at the presence of God, at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
68.9: God, you rained down a shower of blessings, when your heritage was weary you gave it strength.
68.10: Your family found a home, which you in your generosity provided for the humble.
68.11: The Lord gave a command, the good news of a countless army.
68.12: The chieftains of the army are in flight, in flight, and the fair one at home is sharing out the spoils.
68.13: While you are at ease in the sheepfolds, the wings of the Dove are being covered with silver, and her feathers with a sheen of green gold;
68.14: when Shaddai scatters the chieftains, through her it snows on the Dark Mountain.
68.15: A mountain of God, the mountain of Bashan! a haughty mountain, the mountain of Bashan!
68.16: Why be envious, haughty mountains, of the mountain God has chosen for his dwelling? There God will dwell for ever.
68.17: The chariots of God are thousand upon thousand; God has come from Sinai to the sanctuary.
68.18: You have climbed the heights, taken captives, you have taken men as tribute, even rebels that Yahweh God might have a dwelling-place.
68.19: Blessed be the Lord day after day, he carries us along, God our Saviour.Pause
68.20: This God of ours is a God who saves; from Lord Yahweh comes escape from death;
68.21: but God smashes the head of his enemies, the long-haired skull of the prowling criminal.
68.22: The Lord has said, 'I will bring them back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
68.23: so that you may bathe your feet in blood, and the tongues of your dogs feast on your enemies.'
68.24: Your processions, God, are for all to see, the processions of my God, of my king, to the sanctuary;
68.25: singers ahead, musicians behind, in the middle come girls, beating their drums.
68.26: In choirs they bless God, Yahweh, since the foundation of Israel.
68.27: Benjamin was there, the youngest in front, the princes of Judah in bright-coloured robes, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
68.28: Take command, my God, as befits your power, the power, God, which you have wielded for us,
68.29: from your temple high above Jerusalem. Kings will come to you bearing tribute.
68.30: Rebuke the Beast of the Reeds, that herd of bulls, that people of calves, who bow down with ingots of silver. Scatter the people who delight in war.
68.31: From Egypt nobles will come, Ethiopia will stretch out its hands to God.
68.32: Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God, play for
68.33: the Rider of the Heavens, the primeval heavens.Pause There he speaks, with a voice of power!
68.34: Acknowledge the power of God. Over Israel his splendour, in the clouds his power.
68.35: Awesome is God in his sanctuary. He, the God of Israel, gives strength and power to his people. Blessed be God.

69.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'Lilies . . .' Of David] Save me, God, for the waters have closed in on my very being.
69.2: I am sinking in the deepest swamp and there is no firm ground. I have stepped into deep water and the waves are washing over me.
69.3: I am exhausted with calling out, my throat is hoarse, my eyes are worn out with searching for my God.
69.4: More numerous than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without reason. Those who seek to get rid of me are powerful, my treacherous enemies. (Must I give back what I have never stolen?)
69.5: God, you know how foolish I am, my offences are not hidden from you.
69.6: Those who hope in you must not be made fools of, Yahweh Sabaoth, because of me! Those who seek you must not be disgraced, God of Israel, because of me!
69.7: It is for you I bear insults, my face is covered with shame,
69.8: I am estranged from my brothers, alienated from my own mother's sons;
69.9: for I am eaten up with zeal for your house, and insults directed against you fall on me.
69.10: I mortify myself with fasting, and find myself insulted for it,
69.11: I dress myself in sackcloth and become their laughing-stock,
69.12: the gossip of people sitting at the gate, and the theme of drunkards' songs.
69.13: And so, I pray to you, Yahweh, at the time of your favour; in your faithful love answer me, in the constancy of your saving power.
69.14: Rescue me from the mire before I sink in; so I shall be saved from those who hate me, from the watery depths.
69.15: Let not the waves wash over me, nor the deep swallow me up, nor the pit close its mouth on me.
69.16: Answer me, Yahweh, for your faithful love is generous; in your tenderness turn towards me;
69.17: do not turn away from your servant, be quick to answer me, for I am in trouble.
69.18: Come to my side, redeem me, ransom me because of my enemies.
69.19: You know well the insults, the shame and disgrace I endure. Every one of my oppressors is known to you.
69.20: Insult has broken my heart past cure. I hoped for sympathy, but in vain, for consolers -- not one to be found.
69.21: To eat they gave me poison, to drink, vinegar when I was thirsty.
69.22: May their own table prove a trap for them, and their abundance a snare;
69.23: may their eyes grow so dim that they cannot see, all their muscles lose their strength.
69.24: Vent your fury on them, let your burning anger overtake them.
69.25: Reduce their encampment to ruin, and leave their tents untenanted,
69.26: for hounding someone you had already stricken, for redoubling the pain of one you had wounded.
69.27: Charge them with crime after crime, exclude them from your saving justice,
69.28: erase them from the book of life, do not enrol them among the upright.
69.29: For myself, wounded wretch that I am, by your saving power raise me up!
69.30: I will praise God's name in song, I will extol him by thanksgiving,
69.31: for this will please Yahweh more than an ox, than a bullock horned and hoofed.
69.32: The humble have seen and are glad. Let your courage revive, you who seek God.
69.33: For God listens to the poor, he has never scorned his captive people.
69.34: Let heaven and earth and seas, and all that stirs in them, acclaim him!
69.35: For God will save Zion, and rebuild the cities of Judah, and people will live there on their own land;
69.36: the descendants of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell there.

70.1: [For the choirmaster Of David In commemoration] Be pleased, God, to rescue me, Yahweh, come quickly and help me!
70.2: Shame and dismay to those who seek my life! Back with them! Let them be humiliated who delight in my misfortunes.
70.3: Let them shrink away covered with shame, those who say to me, 'Aha, aha!'
70.4: But joy and happiness in you to all who seek you. Let them ceaselessly cry, 'God is great', who love your saving power.
70.5: Poor and needy as I am, God, come quickly to me! Yahweh, my helper, my Saviour, do not delay!

71.1: In you, Yahweh, I take refuge, I shall never be put to shame.
71.2: In your saving justice rescue me, deliver me, listen to me and save me.
71.3: Be a sheltering rock for me, always accessible; you have determined to save me, for you are my rock, my fortress.
71.4: My God, rescue me from the clutches of the wicked, from the grasp of the rogue and the ruthless.
71.5: For you are my hope, Lord, my trust, Yahweh, since boyhood.
71.6: On you I have relied since my birth, since my mother's womb you have been my portion, the constant theme of my praise.
71.7: Many were bewildered at me, but you are my sure refuge.
71.8: My mouth is full of your praises, filled with your splendour all day long.
71.9: Do not reject me in my old age, nor desert me when my strength is failing,
71.10: for my enemies are discussing me, those with designs on my life are plotting together.
71.11: 'Hound him down, for God has deserted him! Seize him, there is no one to rescue him.'
71.12: God, do not stand aloof, my God, come quickly to help me.
71.13: Shame and ruin on those who slander me, may those intent on harming me be covered with insult and infamy.
71.14: As for me, my hope will never fade, I will praise you more and more.
71.15: My lips shall proclaim your saving justice, your saving power all day long.
71.16: I will come in the power of Yahweh to tell of your justice, yours alone.
71.17: God, you have taught me from boyhood, and I am still proclaiming your marvels.
71.18: Now that I am old and grey-haired, God, do not desert me, till I have proclaimed your strength to generations still to come, your power
71.19: and justice to the skies. You have done great things, God, who is like you?
71.20: You have shown me much misery and hardship, but you will give me life again, You will raise me up again from the depths of the earth,
71.21: prolong my old age, and comfort me again.
71.22: For my part, I will thank you on the lyre for your constancy, my God. I will play the harp in your honour, Holy One of Israel.
71.23: My lips sing for joy as I play to you, because you have redeemed me,
71.24: and all day long my tongue muses on your saving justice. Shame and disgrace on those intent to harm me!

72.1: [Of Solomon] God, endow the king with your own fair judgement, the son of the king with your own saving justice,
72.2: that he may rule your people with justice, and your poor with fair judgement.
72.3: Mountains and hills, bring peace to the people! With justice
72.4: he will judge the poor of the people, he will save the children of the needy and crush their oppressors.
72.5: In the sight of the sun and the moon he will endure, age after age.
72.6: He will come down like rain on mown grass, like showers moistening the land.
72.7: In his days uprightness shall flourish, and peace in plenty till the moon is no more.
72.8: His empire shall stretch from sea to sea, from the river to the limits of the earth.
72.9: The Beast will cower before him, his enemies lick the dust;
72.10: the kings of Tarshish and the islands will pay him tribute. The kings of Sheba and Saba will offer gifts;
72.11: all kings will do him homage, all nations become his servants.
72.12: For he rescues the needy who calls to him, and the poor who has no one to help.
72.13: He has pity on the weak and the needy, and saves the needy from death.
72.14: From oppression and violence he redeems their lives, their blood is precious in his sight.
72.15: (Long may he live; may the gold of Sheba be given him!) Prayer will be offered for him constantly, and blessings invoked on him all day.
72.16: May wheat abound in the land, waving on the heights of the hills, like Lebanon with its fruits and flowers at their best, like the grasses of the earth.
72.17: May his name be blessed for ever, and endure in the sight of the sun. In him shall be blessed every race in the world, and all nations call him blessed.
72.18: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, who alone works wonders;
72.19: blessed for ever his glorious name. May the whole world be filled with his glory! Amen! Amen!
72.20: End of the prayers of David, son of Jesse.

73.1: [Psalm Of Asaph] Indeed God is good to Israel, the Lord to those who are pure of heart.
73.2: My feet were on the point of stumbling, a little more and I had slipped,
73.3: envying the arrogant as I did, and seeing the prosperity of the wicked.
73.4: For them no such thing as pain, untroubled, their comfortable portliness;
73.5: exempt from the cares which are the human lot, they have no part in Adam's afflictions.
73.6: So pride is a necklace to them, violence the garment they wear.
73.7: From their fat oozes out malice, their hearts drip with cunning.
73.8: Cynically they advocate evil, loftily they advocate force.
73.9: Their mouth claims heaven for themselves, and their tongue is never still on earth.
73.10: That is why my people turn to them, and enjoy the waters of plenty,
73.11: saying, 'How can God know? What knowledge can the Most High have?'
73.12: That is what the wicked are like, piling up wealth without any worries.
73.13: Was it useless, then, to have kept my own heart clean, to have washed my hands in innocence?
73.14: When I was under a hail of blows all day long, and punished every morning,
73.15: had I said, 'I shall talk like them,' I should have betrayed your children's race.
73.16: So I set myself to understand this: how difficult I found it!
73.17: Until I went into the sanctuaries of the gods and understood what was destined to become of them.
73.18: You place them on a slippery slope and drive them down into chaos.
73.19: How sudden their hideous destruction! They are swept away, annihilated by terror!
73.20: Like a dream upon waking, Lord, when you awake, you dismiss their image.
73.21: My heart grew embittered, my affections dried up,
73.22: I was stupid and uncomprehending, a clumsy animal in your presence.
73.23: Even so, I stayed in your presence, you grasped me by the right hand;
73.24: you will guide me with advice, and will draw me in the wake of your glory.
73.25: Who else is there for me in heaven? And, with you, I lack nothing on earth.
73.26: My heart and my flesh are pining away: my heart's rock, my portion, God for ever!
73.27: Truly, those who abandon you will perish; you destroy those who adulterously desert you,
73.28: whereas my happiness is to be near God. I have made the Lord Yahweh my refuge, to tell of all your works.

74.1: [Poem Of Asaph] God, why have you finally rejected us, your anger blazing against the flock you used to pasture?
74.2: Remember the people you took to yourself long ago, your own tribe which you redeemed, and this Mount Zion where you came to live.
74.3: Come up to these endless ruins! The enemy have sacked everything in the sanctuary;
74.4: your opponents made uproar in the place of assemblies, they fixed their emblems over the entrance, emblems
74.5: never known before. Their axes deep in the wood,
74.6: hacking at the panels, they battered them down with axe and pick;
74.7: they set fire to your sanctuary, profanely rased to the ground the dwelling-place of your name.
74.8: They said to themselves, 'Let us crush them at one stroke!' They burned down every sacred shrine in the land.
74.9: We see no signs, no prophet any more, and none of us knows how long it will last.
74.10: How much longer, God, will the enemy blaspheme? Is the enemy to insult your name for ever?
74.11: Why hold back your hand, keep your right hand hidden in the folds of your robe?
74.12: Yet, God, my king from the first, author of saving acts throughout the earth,
74.13: by your power you split the sea in two, and smashed the heads of the monsters on the waters.
74.14: You crushed Leviathan's heads, gave him as food to the wild animals.
74.15: You released the springs and brooks, and turned primordial rivers into dry land.
74.16: Yours is the day and yours the night, you caused sun and light to exist,
74.17: you fixed all the boundaries of the earth, you created summer and winter.
74.18: Remember, Yahweh, the enemy's blasphemy, a foolish people insults your name.
74.19: Do not surrender your turtledove to the beast; do not forget for ever the life of your oppressed people.
74.20: Look to the covenant! All the hiding-places of the land are full, haunts of violence.
74.21: Do not let the downtrodden retreat in confusion, give the poor and needy cause to praise your name.
74.22: Arise, God, champion your own cause, remember how fools blaspheme you all day long!
74.23: Do not forget the shouting of your enemies, the ever-mounting uproar of your adversaries.

75.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'Do not destroy' Psalm Of Asaph Song] We give thanks to you, God, we give thanks to you, as we call upon your name, as we recount your wonders.
75.2: 'At the appointed time I myself shall dispense justice.
75.3: The earth quakes and all its inhabitants; it is I who hold its pillars firm.Pause
75.4: 'I said to the boastful, "Do not boast!" to the wicked, "Do not flaunt your strength!
75.5: Do not flaunt your strength so proudly, do not talk with that arrogant stance." '
75.6: No longer from east to west, no longer in the mountainous desert,
75.7: is God judging in uprightness, bringing some down, raising others.
75.8: Yahweh is holding a cup filled with a heady blend of wine; he will pour it, they will drink it to the dregs, all the wicked on earth will drink it.
75.9: But I shall speak out for ever, shall make music for the God of Jacob.
75.10: I shall break down all the strength of the wicked, and the strength of the upright will rise high.

76.1: [For the choirmaster For strings Psalm Of Asaph Song] God is acknowledged in Judah, his name is great in Israel,
76.2: his tent is pitched in Salem, his dwelling is in Zion;
76.3: there he has broken the lightning-flashes of the bow, shield and sword and war.Pause
76.4: Radiant you are, and renowned for the mountains of booty
76.5: taken from them. Heroes are now sleeping their last sleep, the warriors' arms have failed them;
76.6: at your reproof, God of Jacob, chariot and horse stand stunned.
76.7: You, you alone, strike terror! Who can hold his ground in your presence when your anger strikes?
76.8: From heaven your verdicts thunder, the earth is silent with dread
76.9: when God takes his stand to give judgement, to save all the humble of the earth.Pause
76.10: Human anger serves only to praise you, the survivors of your anger will huddle round you.
76.11: Make and fulfil your vows to Yahweh your God, let those who surround him make offerings to the Awesome One.
76.12: He cuts short the breath of princes, strikes terror in earthly kings.

77.1: [For the choirmaster . . . Jeduthun Of Asaph Psalm] I cry to God in distress, I cry to God and he hears me.
77.2: In the day of my distress I sought the Lord; all night I tirelessly stretched out my hands, my heart refused to be consoled.
77.3: I sigh as I think of God, my spirit faints away as I ponder on him. Pause
77.4: You kept me from closing my eyes, I was too distraught to speak;
77.5: I thought of former times, years long past
77.6: I recalled; through the night I ponder in my heart, as I reflect, my spirit asks this question:
77.7: Is the Lord's rejection final? Will he never show favour again?
77.8: Is his faithful love gone for ever? Has his Word come to an end for all time?
77.9: Does God forget to show mercy? In anger does he shut off his tenderness?Pause
77.10: And I said, 'This is what wounds me, the right hand of the Most High has lost its strength.'
77.11: Remembering Yahweh's great deeds, remembering your wonders in the past,
77.12: I reflect on all that you did, I ponder all your great deeds.
77.13: God, your ways are holy! What god is as great as our God?
77.14: You are the God who does marvellous deeds, brought nations to acknowledge your power,
77.15: with your own arm redeeming your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph.Pause
77.16: When the waters saw you, God, when the waters saw you they writhed in anguish, the very depths shook with fear.
77.17: The clouds pelted down water, the sky thundered, your arrows shot back and forth.
77.18: The rolling of your thunder was heard, your lightning-flashes lit up the world, the earth shuddered and shook.
77.19: Your way led over the sea, your path over the countless waters, and none could trace your footsteps.
77.20: You guided your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: [Psalm Of Asaph] My people, listen to my teaching, pay attention to what I say.
78.2: I will speak to you in poetry, unfold the mysteries of the past.
78.3: What we have heard and know, what our ancestors have told us
78.4: we shall not conceal from their descendants, but will tell to a generation still to come: the praises of Yahweh, his power, the wonderful deeds he has done.
78.5: He instituted a witness in Jacob, he established a law in Israel, he commanded our ancestors to hand it down to their descendants,
78.6: that a generation still to come might know it, children yet to be born. They should be sure to tell their own children,
78.7: and should put their trust in God, never forgetting God's great deeds, always keeping his commands,
78.8: and not, like their ancestors, be a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation weak of purpose, their spirit fickle towards God.
78.9: The archer sons of Ephraim turned tail when the time came for fighting;
78.10: they failed to keep God's covenant, they refused to follow his Law;
78.11: they had forgotten his great deeds, the marvels he had shown them;
78.12: he did marvels in the sight of their ancestors in Egypt, in the plains of Tanis.
78.13: He split the sea and brought them through, made the waters stand up like a dam;
78.14: he led them with a cloud by day, and all the night with the light of a fire;
78.15: he split rocks in the desert, let them drink as though from the limitless depths;
78.16: he brought forth streams from a rock, made waters flow down in torrents.
78.17: But they only sinned against him more than ever, defying the Most High in barren country;
78.18: they deliberately challenged God by demanding food to their hearts' content.
78.19: They insulted God by saying, 'Can God make a banquet in the desert?
78.20: True, when he struck the rock, waters gushed out and flowed in torrents; but what of bread? Can he give that, can he provide meat for his people?'
78.21: When he heard them Yahweh vented his anger, fire blazed against Jacob, his anger mounted against Israel,
78.22: because they had no faith in God, no trust in his power to save.
78.23: Even so he gave orders to the skies above, he opened the sluice-gates of heaven;
78.24: he rained down manna to feed them, he gave them the wheat of heaven;
78.25: mere mortals ate the bread of the Mighty, he sent them as much food as they could want.
78.26: He roused an east wind in the heavens, despatched a south wind by his strength;
78.27: he rained down meat on them like dust, birds thick as sand on the seashore,
78.28: tumbling into the middle of his camp, all around his dwelling-place.
78.29: They ate as much food as they wanted, he satisfied all their cravings;
78.30: but their cravings were still upon them, the food was still in their mouths,
78.31: when the wrath of God attacked them, slaughtering their strongest men, laying low the flower of Israel.
78.32: Despite all this, they went on sinning, they put no faith in his marvels.
78.33: He made their days vanish in mist, their years in sudden ruin.
78.34: Whenever he slaughtered them, they began to seek him, they turned back and looked eagerly for him,
78.35: recalling that God was their rock, God the Most High, their redeemer.
78.36: They tried to hoodwink him with their mouths, their tongues were deceitful towards him;
78.37: their hearts were not loyal to him, they were not faithful to his covenant.
78.38: But in his compassion he forgave their guilt instead of killing them, time and again repressing his anger instead of rousing his full wrath,
78.39: remembering they were creatures of flesh, a breath of wind that passes, never to return.
78.40: How often they defied him in the desert! How often they grieved him in the wastelands!
78.41: Repeatedly they challenged God, provoking the Holy One of Israel,
78.42: not remembering his hand, the time when he saved them from the oppressor,
78.43: he who did his signs in Egypt, his miracles in the plains of Tanis,
78.44: turning their rivers to blood, their streams so that they had nothing to drink.
78.45: He sent horseflies to eat them up, and frogs to devastate them,
78.46: consigning their crops to the caterpillar, the fruit of their hard work to the locust;
78.47: he killed their vines with hail, their sycamore trees with frost,
78.48: delivering up their cattle to hail, and their flocks to thunderbolts.
78.49: He loosed against them the full heat of his anger, fury, rage and destruction, a detachment of destroying angels;
78.50: he gave free course to his anger. He did not exempt their own selves from death, delivering up their lives to the plague.
78.51: He struck all the first-born in Egypt, the flower of the youth in the tents of Ham.
78.52: He brought out his people like sheep, guiding them like a flock in the desert,
78.53: leading them safe and unafraid, while the sea engulfed their enemies.
78.54: He brought them to his holy land, the hill-country won by his right hand;
78.55: he dispossessed nations before them, measured out a heritage for each of them, and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
78.56: But still they challenged the Most High God and defied him, refusing to keep his decrees;
78.57: as perverse and treacherous as their ancestors, they gave way like a faulty bow,
78.58: provoking him with their high places, rousing his jealousy with their idols.
78.59: God listened and vented his wrath, he totally rejected Israel;
78.60: he forsook his dwelling in Shiloh, the tent where he used to dwell on the earth.
78.61: He abandoned his power to captivity, his splendour to the enemy's clutches;
78.62: he gave up his people to the sword, he vented his wrath on his own heritage.
78.63: Fire devoured their young men, their young girls had no wedding-song;
78.64: their priests fell by the sword and their widows sang no dirge.
78.65: The Lord arose as though he had been asleep, like a strong man fighting-mad with wine,
78.66: he struck his enemies on the rump, and put them to everlasting shame.
78.67: Rejecting the tents of Joseph, passing over the tribe of Ephraim,
78.68: he chose the tribe of Judah, his well-loved mountain of Zion;
78.69: he built his sanctuary like high hills, like the earth set it firm for ever.
78.70: He chose David to be his servant, took him from the sheepfold,
78.71: took him from tending ewes to pasture his servant Jacob, and Israel his heritage.
78.72: He pastured them with unblemished heart, with a sensitive hand he led them.

79.1: [Psalm Of Asaph] God, the pagans have invaded your heritage, they have defiled your holy temple, they have laid Jerusalem in ruins,
79.2: they have left the corpses of your servants as food for the birds of the air, the bodies of your faithful for the wild beasts.
79.3: Around Jerusalem they have shed blood like water, leaving no one to bury them.
79.4: We are the scorn of our neighbours, the butt and laughing-stock of those around us.
79.5: How long will you be angry, Yahweh? For ever? Is your jealousy to go on smouldering like a fire?
79.6: Pour out your anger on the nations who do not acknowledge you, and on the kingdoms that do not call on your name;
79.7: for they have devoured Jacob and devastated his home.
79.8: Do not count against us the guilt of former generations, in your tenderness come quickly to meet us, for we are utterly weakened;
79.9: help us, God our Saviour, for the glory of your name; Yahweh, wipe away our sins, rescue us for the sake of your name.
79.10: Why should the nations ask, 'Where is their God?' Let us see the nations suffer vengeance for shedding your servants' blood.
79.11: May the groans of the captive reach you, by your great strength save those who are condemned to death!
79.12: Repay our neighbours sevenfold for the insults they have levelled at you, Lord.
79.13: And we, your people, the flock that you pasture, will thank you for ever, will recite your praises from age to age.

80.1: [For the choirmaster Tune: 'The decrees are lilies' Of Asaph Psalm] Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like a flock, enthroned on the winged creatures, shine forth
80.2: over Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh; rouse your valour and come to our help.
80.3: God, bring us back, let your face shine on us and we shall be safe.
80.4: Yahweh, God Sabaoth, how long will you flare up at your people's prayer?
80.5: You have made tears their food, redoubled tears their drink.
80.6: You let our neighbours quarrel over us, our enemies mock us.
80.7: God Sabaoth, bring us back, let your face shine on us and we shall be safe.
80.8: You brought a vine out of Egypt, to plant it you drove out nations;
80.9: you cleared a space for it, it took root and filled the whole country.
80.10: The mountains were covered with its shade, and the cedars of God with its branches,
80.11: its boughs stretched as far as the sea, its shoots as far as the River.
80.12: Why have you broken down its fences? Every passer-by plucks its grapes,
80.13: boars from the forest tear at it, wild beasts feed on it.
80.14: God Sabaoth, come back, we pray, look down from heaven and see, visit this vine;
80.15: protect what your own hand has planted.
80.16: They have thrown it on the fire like dung, the frown of your rebuke will destroy them.
80.17: May your hand protect those at your side, the child of Adam you have strengthened for yourself!
80.18: Never again will we turn away from you, give us life and we will call upon your name.
80.19: God Sabaoth, bring us back, let your face shine on us and we shall be safe.

81.1: [For the choirmaster On the . . . of Gath Of Asaph] Sing for joy to God our strength, shout in triumph to the God of Jacob.
81.2: Strike up the music, beat the tambourine, play the melodious harp and the lyre;
81.3: blow the trumpet for the new month, for the full moon, for our feast day!
81.4: For Israel has this statute, a decision of the God of Jacob,
81.5: a decree he imposed on Joseph, when he went to war against Egypt. I heard a voice unknown to me,
81.6: 'I freed his shoulder from the burden, his hands were able to lay aside the labourer's basket.
81.7: You cried out in your distress, so I rescued you. 'Hidden in the storm, I answered you, I tested you at the waters of Meribah.Pause
81.8: Listen, my people, while I give you warning; Israel, if only you would listen to me!
81.9: 'You shall have no strange gods, shall worship no alien god.
81.10: I, Yahweh, am your God, who brought you here from Egypt, you have only to open your mouth for me to fill it.
81.11: 'My people would not listen to me, Israel would have none of me.
81.12: So I left them to their stubborn selves, to follow their own devices.
81.13: 'If only my people would listen to me, if only Israel would walk in my ways,
81.14: at one stroke I would subdue their enemies, turn my hand against their opponents.
81.15: 'Those who hate Yahweh would woo his favour, though their doom was sealed for ever,
81.16: while I would feed him on pure wheat, would give you your fill of honey from the rock.'

82.1: [Psalm Of Asaph] God takes his stand in the divine assembly, surrounded by the gods he gives judgement.
82.2: 'How much longer will you give unjust judgements and uphold the prestige of the wicked?
82.3: Let the weak and the orphan have justice, be fair to the wretched and the destitute.Pause
82.4: 'Rescue the weak and the needy, save them from the clutches of the wicked.
82.5: 'Ignorant and uncomprehending, they wander in darkness, while the foundations of the world are tottering.
82.6: I had thought, "Are you gods, are all of you sons of the Most High?"
82.7: No! you will die as human beings do, as one man, princes, you will fall.'
82.8: Arise, God, judge the world, for all nations belong to you.

83.1: [Song Psalm Of Asaph] God, do not remain silent, do not stay quiet or unmoved, God!
83.2: See how your enemies are in uproar, how those who hate you are rearing their heads.
83.3: They are laying plans against your people, conspiring against those you cherish;
83.4: they say, 'Come, let us annihilate them as a nation, the name of Israel shall be remembered no more!'
83.5: They conspire with a single mind, they conclude an alliance against you,
83.6: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
83.7: Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, Philistia and the Tyrians;
83.8: even Assyria has joined them to reinforce the children of Lot.Pause
83.9: Treat them like Midian and Sisera, like Jabin at the river Kishon;
83.10: wiped out at En-Dor, they served to manure the ground.
83.11: Treat their leaders like Oreb and Zeeb, all their commanders like Zebah and Zalmunna,
83.12: for they said, 'Let us take for ourselves God's settlements.'
83.13: My God, treat them like thistledown, like chaff at the mercy of the wind.
83.14: As fire devours a forest, as a flame sets mountains ablaze,
83.15: so drive them away with your tempest, by your whirlwind fill them with terror.
83.16: Shame written all over their faces, let them seek your name, Yahweh!
83.17: Dishonour and terror be always theirs, death also and destruction.
83.18: Let them know that you alone bear the name of Yahweh, Most High over all the earth.

84.1: [For the choirmaster On the . . . of Gath Of the sons of Korah Psalm] How lovely are your dwelling- places, Yahweh Sabaoth.
84.2: My whole being yearns and pines for Yahweh's courts, My heart and my body cry out for joy to the living God.
84.3: Even the sparrow has found a home, the swallow a nest to place its young: your altars, Yahweh Sabaoth, my King and my God.
84.4: How blessed are those who live in your house; they shall praise you continually. Pause
84.5: Blessed those who find their strength in you, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
84.6: As they pass through the Valley of the Balsam, they make there a water-hole, and -- a further blessing -- early rain fills it.
84.7: They make their way from height to height, God shows himself to them in Zion.
84.8: Yahweh, God Sabaoth, hear my prayer, listen, God of Jacob.
84.9: God, our shield, look, and see the face of your anointed.
84.10: Better one day in your courts than a thousand at my own devices, to stand on the threshold of God's house than to live in the tents of the wicked.
84.11: For Yahweh God is a rampart and shield, he gives grace and glory; Yahweh refuses nothing good to those whose life is blameless.
84.12: Yahweh Sabaoth, blessed is he who trusts in you.

85.1: [For the choirmaster Of the sons of Korah Psalm] Yahweh, you are gracious to your land, you bring back the captives of Jacob,
85.2: you take away the guilt of your people, you blot out all their sin.Pause
85.3: You retract all your anger, you renounce the heat of your fury.
85.4: Bring us back, God our Saviour, appease your indignation against us!
85.5: Will you be angry with us for ever? Will you prolong your wrath age after age?
85.6: Will you not give us life again, for your people to rejoice in you?
85.7: Show us, Lord, your faithful love, grant us your saving help.
85.8: I am listening. What is God's message? Yahweh's message is peace for his people, for his faithful, if only they renounce their folly.
85.9: His saving help is near for those who fear him, his glory will dwell in our land.
85.10: Faithful Love and Loyalty join together, Saving Justice and Peace embrace.
85.11: Loyalty will spring up from the earth, and Justice will lean down from heaven.
85.12: Yahweh will himself give prosperity, and our soil will yield its harvest.
85.13: Justice will walk before him, treading out a path.

86.1: [Prayer Of David] Listen to me, Yahweh, answer me, for I am poor and needy.
86.2: Guard me, for I am faithful, save your servant who relies on you. You are my God,
86.3: take pity on me, Lord, for to you I cry all the day.
86.4: Fill your servant's heart with joy, Lord, for to you I raise up my heart.
86.5: Lord, you are kind and forgiving, rich in faithful love for all who call upon you.
86.6: Yahweh, hear my prayer, listen to the sound of my pleading.
86.7: In my day of distress I call upon you, because you answer me, Lord;
86.8: among the gods there is none to compare with you, no great deeds to compare with yours.
86.9: All nations will come and adore you, Lord, and give glory to your name.
86.10: For you are great and do marvellous deeds, you, God, and none other.
86.11: Teach me, Yahweh, your ways, that I may not stray from your loyalty; let my heart's one aim be to fear your name.
86.12: I thank you with all my heart, Lord my God, I will glorify your name for ever,
86.13: for your faithful love for me is so great that you have rescued me from the depths of Sheol.
86.14: Arrogant men, God, are rising up against me, a brutal gang is after my life, in their scheme of things you have no place.
86.15: But you, Lord, God of tenderness and mercy, slow to anger, rich in faithful love and loyalty,
86.16: turn to me and pity me. Give to your servant your strength, to the child of your servant your saving help,
86.17: give me a sign of your kindness.
86.18: My enemies will see to their shame that you, Yahweh, help and console me.

87.1: [Of the sons of Korah Psalm Song] With its foundations on the holy mountains,
87.2: Yahweh loves his city, he prefers the gates of Zion to any dwelling-place in Jacob.
87.3: He speaks of glory for you, city of God,Pause
87.4: 'I number Rahab and Babylon among those that acknowledge me; look at Tyre, Philistia, Ethiopia, so and so was born there.'
87.5: But of Zion it will be said, 'Every one was born there,' her guarantee is the Most High.
87.6: Yahweh in his register of peoples will note against each, 'Born there',Pause
87.7: princes no less than native-born; all make their home in you.

88.1: [Song Psalm Of the sons of Korah In sickness In suffering Poem For Heman the native-born] Yahweh, God of my salvation, when I cry out to you in the night,
88.2: may my prayer reach your presence, hear my cry for help.
88.3: For I am filled with misery, my life is on the brink of Sheol;
88.4: already numbered among those who sink into oblivion, I am as one bereft of strength,
88.5: left alone among the dead, like the slaughtered lying in the grave, whom you remember no more, cut off as they are from your protection.
88.6: You have plunged me to the bottom of the grave, in the darkness, in the depths;
88.7: weighted down by your anger, kept low by your waves.Pause
88.8: You have deprived me of my friends, made me repulsive to them, imprisoned, with no escape;
88.9: my eyes are worn out with suffering. I call to you, Yahweh, all day, I stretch out my hands to you.
88.10: Do you work wonders for the dead, can shadows rise up to praise you?Pause
88.11: Do they speak in the grave of your faithful love, of your constancy in the place of perdition?
88.12: Are your wonders known in the darkness, your saving justice in the land of oblivion?
88.13: But, for my part, I cry to you, Yahweh, every morning my prayer comes before you;
88.14: why, Yahweh, do you rebuff me, turn your face away from me?
88.15: Wretched and close to death since childhood, I have borne your terrors -- I am finished!
88.16: Your anger has overwhelmed me, your terrors annihilated me.
88.17: They flood around me all day long, close in on me all at once.
88.18: You have deprived me of friends and companions, and all that I know is the dark.

89.1: [Poem For Ethan the native-born] I shall sing the faithful love of Yahweh for ever, from age to age my lips shall declare your constancy,
89.2: for you have said: love is built to last for ever, you have fixed your constancy firm in the heavens.
89.3: 'I have made a covenant with my Chosen One, sworn an oath to my servant David:
89.4: I have made your dynasty firm for ever, built your throne stable age after age.'Pause
89.5: The heavens praise your wonders, Yahweh, your constancy in the gathering of your faithful.
89.6: Who in the skies can compare with Yahweh? Who among the sons of god can rival him?
89.7: God, awesome in the assembly of holy ones, great and dreaded among all who surround him,
89.8: Yahweh, God Sabaoth, who is like you? Mighty Yahweh, your constancy is all round you!
89.9: You control the pride of the ocean, when its waves ride high you calm them.
89.10: You split Rahab in two like a corpse, scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
89.11: Yours are the heavens and yours the earth, the world and all it holds, you founded them;
89.12: you created the north and the south, Tabor and Hermon hail your name with joy.
89.13: Yours is a strong arm, mighty your hand, your right hand raised high;
89.14: Saving Justice and Fair Judgement the foundations of your throne, Faithful Love and Constancy march before you.
89.15: How blessed the nation that learns to acclaim you! They will live, Yahweh, in the light of your presence.
89.16: In your name they rejoice all day long, by your saving justice they are raised up.
89.17: You are the flower of their strength, by your favour our strength is triumphant;
89.18: for to Yahweh belongs our shield, to the Holy One of Israel our king.
89.19: Once you spoke in a vision, to your faithful you said: 'I have given strength to a warrior, I have raised up a man chosen from my people.
89.20: 'I have found David my servant, and anointed him with my holy oil.
89.21: My hand will always be with him, my arm will make him strong.
89.22: 'No enemy will be able to outwit him, no wicked man overcome him;
89.23: I shall crush his enemies before him, strike his opponents dead.
89.24: 'My constancy and faithful love will be with him, in my name his strength will be triumphant.
89.25: I shall establish his power over the sea, his dominion over the rivers.
89.26: 'He will cry to me, "You are my father, my God, the rock of my salvation!"
89.27: So I shall make him my first-born, the highest of earthly kings.
89.28: 'I shall maintain my faithful love for him always, my covenant with him will stay firm.
89.29: I have established his dynasty for ever, his throne to be as lasting as the heavens.
89.30: 'Should his descendants desert my law, and not keep to my rulings,
89.31: should they violate my statutes, and not observe my commandments,
89.32: 'then I shall punish their offences with the rod, their guilt with the whip,
89.33: but I shall never withdraw from him my faithful love, I shall not belie my constancy.
89.34: 'I shall not violate my covenant, I shall not withdraw the word once spoken.
89.35: I have sworn by my holiness, once and for all, never will I break faith with David.
89.36: 'His dynasty shall endure for ever, his throne like the sun before me,
89.37: as the moon is established for ever, a faithful witness in the skies.'Pause
89.38: Yet you yourself -- you have spurned and rejected, and have vented your wrath on your anointed,
89.39: you have repudiated the covenant with your servant, dishonoured his crown in the dust.
89.40: You have pierced all his defences, and laid his strongholds in ruins,
89.41: everyone passing by plunders him, he has become the butt of his neighbours.
89.42: You have raised high the right hand of his opponents, have made all his enemies happy;
89.43: you have snapped off his sword on a rock, and failed to support him in battle.
89.44: You have stripped him of his splendid sceptre, and toppled his throne to the ground.
89.45: You have aged him before his time, enveloped him in shame.Pause
89.46: How long, Yahweh, will you remain hidden? For ever? Is your anger to go on smouldering like a fire?
89.47: Remember me; how long have I left? For what pointless end did you create all the children of Adam?
89.48: Who can live and never see death? Who can save himself from the clutches of Sheol?Pause
89.49: Lord, what of those pledges of your faithful love? You made an oath to David by your constancy.
89.50: Do not forget the insults to your servant; I take to heart the taunts of the nations,
89.51: which your enemies have levelled, Yahweh, have levelled at the footsteps of your anointed!
89.52: Blessed be Yahweh for ever. Amen, Amen.

90.1: [Prayer Of Moses, man of God] Lord, you have been our refuge from age to age.
90.2: Before the mountains were born, before the earth and the world came to birth, from eternity to eternity you are God.
90.3: You bring human beings to the dust, by saying, 'Return, children of Adam.'
90.4: A thousand years are to you like a yesterday which has passed, like a watch of the night.
90.5: You flood them with sleep -- in the morning they will be like growing grass:
90.6: in the morning it is blossoming and growing, by evening it is withered and dry.
90.7: For we have been destroyed by your wrath, dismayed by your anger.
90.8: You have taken note of our guilty deeds, our secrets in the full light of your presence.
90.9: All our days pass under your wrath, our lives are over like a sigh.
90.10: The span of our life is seventy years -- eighty for those who are strong -- but their whole extent is anxiety and trouble, they are over in a moment and we are gone.
90.11: Who feels the power of your anger, or who that fears you, your wrath?
90.12: Teach us to count up the days that are ours, and we shall come to the heart of wisdom.
90.13: Come back, Yahweh! How long must we wait? Take pity on your servants.
90.14: Each morning fill us with your faithful love, we shall sing and be happy all our days;
90.15: let our joy be as long as the time that you afflicted us, the years when we experienced disaster.
90.16: Show your servants the deeds you do, let their children enjoy your splendour!
90.17: May the sweetness of the Lord be upon us, to confirm the work we have done!

91.1: You who live in the secret place of Elyon, spend your nights in the shelter of Shaddai,
91.2: saying to Yahweh, 'My refuge, my fortress, my God in whom I trust!'
91.3: He rescues you from the snare of the fowler set on destruction;
91.4: he covers you with his pinions, you find shelter under his wings. His constancy is shield and protection.
91.5: You need not fear the terrors of night, the arrow that flies in the daytime,
91.6: the plague that stalks in the darkness, the scourge that wreaks havoc at high noon.
91.7: Though a thousand fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand, you yourself will remain unscathed.
91.8: You have only to keep your eyes open to see how the wicked are repaid,
91.9: you who say, 'Yahweh my refuge!' and make Elyon your fortress.
91.10: No disaster can overtake you, no plague come near your tent;
91.11: he has given his angels orders about you to guard you wherever you go.
91.12: They will carry you in their arms in case you trip over a stone.
91.13: You will walk upon wild beast and adder, you will trample young lions and snakes.
91.14: 'Since he clings to me I rescue him, I raise him high, since he acknowledges my name.
91.15: He calls to me and I answer him: in distress I am at his side, I rescue him and bring him honour.
91.16: I shall satisfy him with long life, and grant him to see my salvation.'

92.1: [Psalm Song For the Sabbath] It is good to give thanks to Yahweh, to make music for your name, Most High,
92.2: to proclaim your faithful love at daybreak, and your constancy all through the night,
92.3: on the lyre, the ten-stringed lyre, to the murmur of the harp.
92.4: You have brought me joy, Yahweh, by your deeds, at the work of your hands I cry out,
92.5: 'How great are your works, Yahweh, immensely deep your thoughts!'
92.6: Stupid people cannot realise this, fools do not grasp it.
92.7: The wicked may sprout like weeds, and every evil-doer flourish, but only to be eternally destroyed;
92.8: whereas you are supreme for ever, Yahweh.
92.9: Look how your enemies perish, how all evil-doers are scattered!
92.10: You give me the strength of the wild ox, you anoint me with fresh oil;
92.11: I caught sight of the ambush against me, overheard the plans of the wicked.
92.12: The upright will flourish like the palm tree, will grow like a cedar of Lebanon.
92.13: Planted in the house of Yahweh, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
92.14: In old age they will still bear fruit, will remain fresh and green,
92.15: to proclaim Yahweh's integrity; my rock, in whom no fault can be found.

93.1: Yahweh is king, robed in majesty, robed is Yahweh and girded with power.
93.2: The world is indeed set firm, it can never be shaken; your throne is set firm from of old, from all eternity you exist.
93.3: The rivers lift up, Yahweh, the rivers lift up their voices, the rivers lift up their thunder.
93.4: Greater than the voice of many waters, more majestic than the breakers of the sea, Yahweh is majestic in the heights.
93.5: Your decrees stand firm, unshakeable, holiness is the beauty of your house, Yahweh, for all time to come.

94.1: God of vengeance, Yahweh, God of vengeance, shine forth!
94.2: Arise, judge of the world, give back the proud what they deserve!
94.3: How long are the wicked, Yahweh, how long are the wicked to triumph?
94.4: They bluster and boast, they flaunt themselves, all the evil-doers.
94.5: They crush your people, Yahweh, they oppress your heritage,
94.6: they murder the widow and the stranger, bring the orphan to a violent death.
94.7: They say, 'Yahweh is not looking, the God of Jacob is taking no notice.'
94.8: Take notice yourselves, you coarsest of people! Fools, when will you learn some sense?
94.9: Shall he who implanted the ear not hear, he who fashioned the eye not see?
94.10: Shall he who instructs nations not punish? Yahweh, the teacher of all people,
94.11: knows human plans and how insipid they are.
94.12: How blessed are those you instruct, Yahweh, whom you teach by means of your law,
94.13: to give them respite in evil times, till a pit is dug for the wicked.
94.14: Yahweh will not abandon his people, he will not desert his heritage;
94.15: for judgement will again become saving justice, and in its wake all upright hearts will follow.
94.16: Who rises up on my side against the wicked? Who stands firm on my side against all evil-doers?
94.17: If Yahweh did not come to my help, I should soon find myself dwelling in the silence.
94.18: I need only say, 'I am slipping,' for your faithful love, Yahweh, to support me;
94.19: however great the anxiety of my heart, your consolations soothe me.
94.20: Are you partner to a destructive court, that gives disorder the status of law?
94.21: They make an attack on the life of the upright, and condemn innocent blood.
94.22: No! Yahweh is a stronghold to me, my God is my rock of refuge.
94.23: He turns back their guilt on themselves, annihilates them for their wickedness, he annihilates them, Yahweh our God.

95.1: Come, let us cry out with joy to Yahweh, acclaim the rock of our salvation.
95.2: Let us come into his presence with thanksgiving, acclaim him with music.
95.3: For Yahweh is a great God, a king greater than all the gods.
95.4: In his power are the depths of the earth, the peaks of the mountains are his;
95.5: the sea belongs to him, for he made it, and the dry land, moulded by his hands.
95.6: Come, let us bow low and do reverence; kneel before Yahweh who made us!
95.7: For he is our God, and we the people of his sheepfold, the flock of his hand. If only you would listen to him today!
95.8: Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as at the time of Massah in the desert,
95.9: when your ancestors challenged me, put me to the test, and saw what I could do!
95.10: For forty years that generation sickened me, and I said, 'Always fickle hearts; they cannot grasp my ways.'
95.11: Then in my anger I swore they would never enter my place of rest.

96.1: Sing a new song to Yahweh! Sing to Yahweh, all the earth!
96.2: Sing to Yahweh, bless his name! Proclaim his salvation day after day,
96.3: declare his glory among the nations, his marvels to every people!
96.4: Great is Yahweh, worthy of all praise, more awesome than any of the gods.
96.5: All the gods of the nations are idols! It was Yahweh who made the heavens;
96.6: in his presence are splendour and majesty, in his sanctuary power and beauty.
96.7: Give to Yahweh, families of nations, give to Yahweh glory and power,
96.8: give to Yahweh the glory due to his name! Bring an offering and enter his courts,
96.9: adore Yahweh in the splendour of his holiness. Tremble before him, all the earth.
96.10: Say among the nations, 'Yahweh is king.' The world is set firm, it cannot be moved. He will judge the nations with justice.
96.11: Let the heavens rejoice and earth be glad! Let the sea thunder, and all it holds!
96.12: Let the countryside exult, and all that is in it, and all the trees of the forest cry out for joy,
96.13: at Yahweh's approach, for he is coming, coming to judge the earth; he will judge the world with saving justice, and the nations with constancy.

97.1: Yahweh is king! Let earth rejoice, the many isles be glad!
97.2: Cloud, black cloud enfolds him, saving justice and judgement the foundations of his throne.
97.3: Fire goes before him, sets ablaze his enemies all around;
97.4: his lightning-flashes light up the world, the earth sees it and quakes.
97.5: The mountains melt like wax, before the Lord of all the earth.
97.6: The heavens proclaim his saving justice, all nations see his glory.
97.7: Shame on all who serve images, who pride themselves on their idols; bow down to him, all you gods!
97.8: Zion hears and is glad, the daughters of Judah exult, because of your judgements, Yahweh.
97.9: For you are Yahweh, Most High over all the earth, far transcending all gods.
97.10: Yahweh loves those who hate evil, he keeps safe his faithful, rescues them from the clutches of the wicked.
97.11: Light dawns for the upright, and joy for honest hearts.
97.12: Rejoice in Yahweh, you who are upright, praise his unforgettable holiness.

98.1: [Psalm] Sing a new song to Yahweh, for he has performed wonders, his saving power is in his right hand and his holy arm.
98.2: Yahweh has made known his saving power, revealed his saving justice for the nations to see,
98.3: mindful of his faithful love and his constancy to the House of Israel. The whole wide world has seen the saving power of our God.
98.4: Acclaim Yahweh, all the earth, burst into shouts of joy!
98.5: Play to Yahweh on the harp, to the sound of instruments;
98.6: to the sound of trumpet and horn, acclaim the presence of the King.
98.7: Let the sea thunder, and all that it holds, the world and all who live in it.
98.8: Let the rivers clap their hands, and the mountains shout for joy together,
98.9: at Yahweh's approach, for he is coming to judge the earth; he will judge the world with saving justice and the nations with fairness.

99.1: Yahweh is king, the peoples tremble; he is enthroned on the winged creatures, the earth shivers;
99.2: Yahweh is great in Zion. He is supreme over all nations;
99.3: let them praise your name, great and awesome; holy is he
99.4: and mighty! You are a king who loves justice, you established honesty, justice and uprightness; in Jacob it is you who are active.
99.5: Exalt Yahweh our God, bow down at his footstool; holy is he!
99.6: Moses and Aaron are among his priests, and Samuel, calling on his name; they called on Yahweh and he answered them.
99.7: He spoke with them in the pillar of fire, they obeyed his decrees, the Law he gave them.
99.8: Yahweh our God, you answered them, you were a God of forgiveness to them, but punished them for their sins.
99.9: Exalt Yahweh our God, bow down at his holy mountain; holy is Yahweh our God!

100.1: [Psalm For thanksgiving] Acclaim Yahweh, all the earth,
100.2: serve Yahweh with gladness, come into his presence with songs of joy!
100.3: Be sure that Yahweh is God, he made us, we belong to him, his people, the flock of his sheepfold.
100.4: Come within his gates giving thanks, to his courts singing praise, give thanks to him and bless his name!
100.5: For Yahweh is good, his faithful love is everlasting, his constancy from age to age.

101.1: [Of David Psalm] I will sing of faithful love and judgement; to you, Yahweh, will I make music.
101.2: I will go forward in the path of the blameless; when will you come to me? I will live in purity of heart, in my house,
101.3: I will not set before my eyes anything sordid. I hate those who act crookedly; this has no attraction for me.
101.4: Let the perverse of heart keep away from me; the wicked I disregard.
101.5: One who secretly slanders a comrade, I reduce to silence; haughty looks, proud heart, these I cannot abide.
101.6: I look to the faithful of the land to be my companions, only he who walks in the path of the blameless shall be my servant.
101.7: There is no room in my house for anyone who practises deceit; no liar will stand his ground where I can see him.
101.8: Morning after morning I reduce to silence all the wicked in the land, banishing from the city of Yahweh all evil-doers.

102.1: [Prayer of someone afflicted, who in misfortune pours out sorrows before Yahweh] Yahweh, hear my prayer, let my cry for help reach you.
102.2: Do not turn away your face from me when I am in trouble; bend down and listen to me, when I call, be quick to answer me!
102.3: For my days are vanishing like smoke, my bones burning like an oven;
102.4: like grass struck by blight, my heart is withering, I forget to eat my meals.
102.5: From the effort of voicing my groans my bones stick out through my skin.
102.6: I am like a desert-owl in the wastes, a screech-owl among ruins,
102.7: I keep vigil and moan like a lone bird on a roof.
102.8: All day long my enemies taunt me, those who once praised me now use me as a curse.
102.9: Ashes are the food that I eat, my drink is mingled with tears,
102.10: because of your fury and anger, since you have raised me up only to cast me away;
